description: The coronary sinus and its tributaries constitute the anatomical foundation for successful cardiac resynchronization therapy. Despite the emergence of conduction system pacing as a physiological alternative, conventional transvenous CRT retains its important role—not all clinical scenarios can be addressed by left bundle branch area or His bundle pacing alone. Understanding coronary venous anatomy therefore remains essential for every implanting physician.

title: Surgery versus stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic colorectal cancer: a prospective cohort study with propensity score matching
creator: Daohai Wang, Zhili Zhao, Weijie Zhao, Guanglong Chen, Wei Du, Zhi Li, Jian Zhang
description: BackgroundThe optimal local therapy for oligometastatic colorectal cancer (CRC) remains undefined, with radical surgical resection and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) serving as the primary modalities. High-quality comparative evidence is scarce. This study aimed to prospectively compare overall survival (OS), local tumor control (LTC), quality of life (QoL), adverse events, and healthcare resource utilization between these two treatments.

title: Enhancement of the activity of scorpion short-chain antimicrobial peptides by addition of basic residues at the C-terminus
creator: Alhussin Mohamed Abdelhakeem Megaly, Amal Mokhtar, Mohammed Abdel-Wahab, Yoshiaki Nakagawa, Masahiro Miyashita
description: Scorpion venom contains antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These AMPs are classified into three families based on peptide length: long-chain (>35 residues), intermediate-chain (20–35 residues), and short-chain (13–19 residues) AMPs. Previously, we identified both short- and intermediate-chain AMPs from the venom of the scorpion Isometrus maculatus.

title: Unraveling impaired awareness: experiences of people with dementia, Huntington’s disease and Korsakoff’s syndrome, and their informal caregivers
creator: Hester Fidder, Esther de Groot, Marike E. de Boer, Marina R. Ekkel, Ruth B. Veenhuizen, Martin Smalbrugge, Anouk M. van Loon
description: BackgroundImpaired awareness occurs in people with dementia (DEM; Alzheimer’s disease (AD), including mixed AD/vascular), Huntington’s disease (HD) and Korsakoff’s syndrome (KS). We explored the experiences of these people and their informal caregivers, to gain a better understanding of this phenomenon.

title: Dietary advanced glycation end products intake and osteoporosis risk in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
creator: Liping Jin, Qing Liu, Shuai Qin, Lu Gan, Xiaoqiong Chen, Mei Mo, Jialu Liao, Yuanyuan Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Advanced glycation end products (AGEs) derived from dietary sources may aggravate metabolic inflammation and impair bone turnover in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM); however, clinical evidence linking dietary AGEs exposure to osteoporosis (OS) in T2DM remains limited. In this retrospective cohort study, 200 adults with T2DM treated at a tertiary hospital between January 2020 and December 2022 were included.

title: Regioselective synthesis of 3-halo-2H-chromenes via decarboxylative halogenation of oxygenated 3-carboxy-2H-chromenes: Application to isoflavonoid synthesis
creator: Bubwoong Kang, Kosuke Takahara, Itsuki Toyoguchi, Tetsuya Satoh
description: A practical and regioselective method has been developed for 3-halo-2H-chromene synthesis via decarboxylative halogenation. These chromenes are key intermediates in synthesizing isoflavene derivatives and related bioactive compounds, including molecules of interest in agrochemical research. In this study, 3-carboxy-2H-chromenes, prepared from salicylaldehyde-derived cyanochromenes, were subjected to decarboxylative halogenation under mild conditions.

title: Correction: Intraoperative precision of 25-gauge beveled-tip versus 23-gauge flat-tip probes in day surgery vitrectomy for proliferative diabetic retinopathy: a comparative cohort study
creator: Daxi Xue, Yanchun Zhang, Ziwei Kang, Jiamin Zheng, Yingnan He, Xin Luo
description:

title: Association of Life’s Crucial 9 with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among the individuals with chronic inflammatory airway diseases
creator: Youli Wen, Wenqiang Li, Jingshan Bai, Guojie Teng, Yanlei Ge, Yuting Fan, Qian Huang
description: Patients with chronic inflammatory airway diseases (CIAD) have been found to carry a higher burden of cardiovascular diseases. The objective of our research is to explore the link between Life’s Crucial 9 (LC9), a newly introduced measure of cardiovascular health by the American Heart Association, and the risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality among patients with CIAD.

title: CaliciBoost: Performance-driven evaluation of molecular representations for caco-2 permeability prediction
creator: Huong Van Le, Weibin Ren, Junhong Kim, Yukyung Yun, Young Bin Park, Young Jun Kim, Bok Kyung Han, Inho Choi, Jong-Il Park, Hwi-yeol Yun, Jae-Mun Choi
description: AbstractCaco-2= permeability serves as a critical in vitro indicator for predicting the oral absorption of drug candidates= during early-stage drug discovery. To enhance the accuracy and= efficiency of computational predictions, we systematically investigated the impact of eight molecular feature= representation types including 2D/3D descriptors, structural fingerprints, and deep learning-based embeddings combined with automated machine learning techniques to predict Caco-2 permeability.

title: Deep Prior Framework: integrating functional specificity with general plausibility for targeted protein evolution
creator: Senxin Zhang, Yining Qin, Hanwen Zhu, Feilong Meng, Lei Jia, Xiaoqi Zheng
description: The efficiency of directed protein evolution largely relies on computational methods to enrich mutants with high fitness. Traditional strategies, such as zero-shot approaches based on Protein Language Models (PLMs), primarily leverage general “plausibility” priors learned from natural sequences. However, in the absence of experimental feedback, their ability to guide evolution toward specific functions (“specificity”) remains limited.

title: Discrete subaortic stenosis: prognostic value of the left ventricular outflow tract gradient and implications for earlier surgical intervention
creator: Yu-Tong Jiang, Ting-Ting Zhang, Li Zhang, Nan Xu, Bing Zhang, Jia-Qi Zhang, Ke-Ming Yang, Shou-Jun Li, Kun-Jing Pang
description: BackgroundThe optimal timing of surgery for discrete subaortic stenosis (DSS) is controversial due to limited evidence from large-scale trials. This study aimed to identify prognostic factors and reassess current surgical thresholds.MethodsA total of 508 patients with DSS, including 375 pediatric patients, who underwent surgery at a single tertiary center between May 2018 and March 2025 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Application of a structured perianal skin protection protocol incorporating individualized nutritional support for incontinence-associated dermatitis in active Crohn’s disease patients with diarrhea
creator: Yan Zeng, Mei Huang, Wenfang Hu, Yan Wu
description: This study evaluates the effect of a structured perianal skin protection protocol based on individualized nutritional intervention on diarrhea-related incontinence-associated dermatitis (IAD) in patients with active Crohn’s disease (CD). This retrospective cohort study included 200 active CD patients with diarrhea admitted from January 2023 to December 2025.

title: Left ventricular hypertrabeculation is a novel predictor of life-threatening arrhythmic events in long QT syndrome patients
creator: Jing Yang, Kun Li, Fang Liu, Lingyun Kong, Yuanwei Liu, Fei She, Rong He, Tingting Lv, Fulan Liu, Ping Zhang
description: BackgroundLong QT syndrome (LQTS) is a malignant cardiac channelopathy for patients with traditionally normal heart structures. Sporadic cases reported left ventricular hypertrabeculation (LVHT) was a deadly double hit in LQTS patients. Here we summarize the prevalence of LVHT within LQTS subjects and analyse the correlation of LVHT with life-threatening arrhythmic events (LAEs).

title: Multi-criteria decision analysis and linear programming for optimal resource allocation in water quality monitoring networks: a case study of California’s EPA monitoring stations
creator: Hugo Pimentel Tavares, Nilo Antônio de Souza Sampaio
description: Water quality monitoring networks require strategic resource allocation to maximize effectiveness while managing budget constraints. This study presents an integrated multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework combining CRITIC (CRiteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation), TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution), VIKOR (VIseKriterijumska Optimizacija I Kompromisno Resenje), and linear programming (LP) optimization for prioritizing monitoring stations and allocating resources.

title: Post-cannulation prognostic reassessment in ECPR
creator: Taekwon Kim, Sang-hun Lee, Kyungsub Song, Jonghoon Yoo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Static prognostic scores for extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation have been developed for pre-cannulation risk estimation and are frequently repurposed for post-cannulation decisions, where early treatment response may be more informative. We evaluated 3 widely used pre extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) scores (TiPS65, RESCUE-in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA), and Survival After Veno-Arterial ECMO) for in-hospital mortality in a single-center cohort of 158 adults treated with extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (2015-2022).

title: Using context mapping for planning implementation of movement behavior change in physiotherapy
creator: Sofie van Rongen, Joan M Dallinga, Anita Feleus, Ingrid Rosbergen, Alice Schut, Myrenka Bik, Petra Siemonsma, Sanne I de Vries, Arlette E Hesselink
description: BackgroundPhysiotherapists often lack a comprehensive understanding of self-management and encounter challenges in providing self-management support. The Keep Moving Support Tool (KMST) was developed to support physiotherapists in their role as health promotors and to stimulate physical activity in patients with (risk of) chronic conditions.

title: Successful treatment of a large-sized triple-negative breast cancer
creator: Dong Zeng, Xiaolan Liu, Shenya Fu, Zhen Liu, Xuezhu Zhao, Luo Zhong, Xiaohui Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rationale:Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is defined as the absence of estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor expression, along with a lack of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 overexpression or amplification. Patients with TNBC exhibit a poorer prognosis, characterized by a higher propensity for metastasis to the lungs, liver, and brain, and a lower overall survival rate than other breast cancer subtypes. Primary treatment modalities for TNBC include surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy.

title: The dynamics of rare earth elements in soil–plant systems in southern Brazil: a case study of carbonatite-bearing areas and Baccharis trimera
creator: Lucas Mironuk Frescura, Nicole Werle da Silva, Daniel Triboli Vieira, Maria Luiza de Vargas Mallmann, Edinei Koester, Rogerio Vescia Lourega, Marcelo Barcellos da Rosa
description: Carbonatite outcrops represent significant global sources of rare earth elements (REEs). However, their influence on surrounding soils, vegetation, and REE biogeochemical cycling remains insufficiently understood, particularly in Brazilian carbonatite-bearing systems. Hence, this study investigated the distribution and transfer of REEs in soils and Baccharis trimera near two carbonatite bodies in Caçapava do Sul (Rio Grande do Sul State, southernmost Brazil).

title: A qualitative exploration of gender-based violence throughout the migration journey among refugee women in Nairobi, Kenya
creator: Lena Moraa Obara, Edward J Alessi, Chiara Sabina, Samantha C Winter, Rachel John, Aishworya Shrestha, Gi Un Shin, Victoria Banyard
description: BackgroundGender-based violence (GBV) is a serious public health issue and violation of human rights that disproportionately impacts refugee women. This qualitative study explores GBV among urban refugee women in Nairobi, Kenya, using the migration process framework (Zimmerman C, Kiss L, Hossain M, PLoS Med 8: e1001034-e1001034, 2011) to explore violence across the migration journey (i.e.

title: Acute kidney injury is associated with decreased platelet function in domestic cats
creator: Matthew R Kornya, Shauna L Blois, Anthony C G Abrams-Ogg
description: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with platelet dysfunction in several species, but has been minimally investigated in cats. The Platelet Function Analyzer-200 (PFA-200) and Multiplate® (MP) investigate platelet function using different mechanisms.Hypothesis/ObjectivesCats with AKI will show evidence of platelet dysfunction on PFA-200 collagen/adenosine diphosphate (Col/ADP) and MP ADP, Col, and arachidonic acid (ASPI) assays.

title: Ectopic parathyroid adenoma: successful localization with 18F-fluorocholine PET/CT and parathyroid venous sampling in two cases
creator: Byungkwan Jung, Yoochan Shin, Sungahn Lee, Namki Hong, Sang Yu Nam, Sihoon Lee
description: BackgroundClinically suspected parathyroid adenomas, which are not localized by conventional imaging such as ultrasonography and technetium-99 m (99mTc) sestamibi scintigraphy, remain challenging. We describe two patients with hypercalcemia and elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) levels, in whom ultrasonography or technetium-99 m sestamibi scintigraphy failed to identify the lesions.

title: Outpatient surgical referrals from primary care providers for people experiencing homelessness: a retrospective review
creator: Madeline McDonald, Peter Huan, Caroline Hircock, Christina Pizzola, Timothy O’Shea, Carolyn Lévis, Margherita Cadeddu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:People experiencing homelessness suffer from a high burden of surgical conditions and face many barriers to accessing care. Our aim was to describe the unmeasured and unmet need of surgical care through outpatient surgical referrals.Methods:This is a retrospective review of electronic patient charts from the Shelter Health Network, a health care and social service organization serving people experiencing homelessness in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.

title: The impact of dynamic neuromuscular stabilization on postural control and balance in post-stroke patients with sarcopenia
creator: Jie Zhuang, Dorota Duhova, Lei Song, Juan Jin, Tingting Meng, Mengxue Sun, Zekai Hu, Yimeng Xu, Yimin Shen, Junwen Long, Jue Wang, Yueren Liu, Wenshu Guo, Jin Hu, Fen Rao, Lei Fang
description: Rationale:The coexistence of stroke and sarcopenia increases the risk of functional decline, falls, and disability. Dynamic Neuromuscular Stabilization (DNS) emphasizes diaphragmatic breathing, intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) regulation, and coordinated stabilizer activity; however, its role in post-stroke patients with sarcopenia remains uncertain.

title: Idiopathic unilateral vortex vein dilation: a multimodal imaging case report
creator: Xiaohui Tian, Leibing Ji, Reyisai Abudulamu
description: PurposeTo report a case of idiopathic vortex vein dilatation diagnosed using multimodal imaging, including indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), sodium fluorescein angiography (FFA), wide-angle color fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), and ocular ultrasound.MethodsVortex vein dilatation is a clinically rare phenomenon, often incidentally detected during imaging. Its characteristic fundus appearance can mimic choroidal tumors or vascular lesions, potentially leading to unnecessary intervention.

title: Radiation therapy, cytogenetic prognostication, novel systemic chemotherapy, and patient perspective in an adult with choroidal melanoma
creator: Kevin Card, Rizwan Haq, John Mignano, Shilpa J Desai
description: ng neurosensory retina) and to return as needed. Her past medical history was notable only for hypertension and hyperlipidemia. Her family history was negative for malignancy. She had an active prior history of smoking with a 29‐pack‐year history and was consuming one pack per day.

title: Association between malocclusion severity and social anxiety, self-esteem in adolescents
creator: Wanjun Zhang, Yongping Ma, Yanming Guo, Qian Yang, Zhen Da
description: This study investigates the association between malocclusion severity and social anxiety and self-esteem levels in adolescents and explores factors associated with heterogeneity in these psychological outcomes. A cross-sectional study design was employed. A convenience sample of 190 adolescents aged 12 to 18 years, recruited from the orthodontic department of a hospital from June 2023 to December 2025, was enrolled.

title: Shared decision-making with older people on TReatment Escalation planning for Acute deterioration in the emergency Medical Setting - Observed (STREAMS-O): an ethnographic study
creator: Bronwen E. Warner, Mary Wells, Cecilia Vindrola-Padros, Stephen J. Brett
description: BackgroundShared decision-making is increasingly expected in healthcare. Treatment escalation planning is a contingency for medical intervention in the event of acute deterioration in hospital. Treatment escalation planning guidelines in the United Kingdom reference shared decision-making but it is not clear to what extent this is feasible.

title: High-urgency heart transplantation and outcome trade-offs: early post-transplant infection and mortality
creator: Kyu-Sun Lee, Darae Kim, Jin-Oh Choi, Hae-Young Lee, Myoung Soo Kim, Hyungseop Kim, Dong-Ju Choi, Sang Eun Lee, Seok-Min Kang, Soo Yong Lee, Hyun-Jai Cho, Cheol Kim, Cheol Kim, Jaewon Oh, Jin Joo Park, Min Ho Ju, Sung Ho Jung, Jung Ae Hong, Jeehoon Kang, Jeongsu Kim, Junho Hyun, Mi Hee Lim, Minjae Yo
description: Background and AimsTo evaluate differences in post-transplant outcomes by pre-transplant urgency status, focusing on early post-transplant infection and its contribution to mortality.MethodsWe retrospectively analysed 801 adult heart transplant recipients enrolled in the Korea Organ Transplant Registry (April 2014–December 2021). Recipients were classified as Status 0 (highest urgency; n = 287) and Status 1–3 (n = 514).

title: Unveiling complete genome sequence of Streptomyces griseoincarnatus AR2 from Katpana cold desert: the roof of the world surrounded by Karakoram mountain range
creator: Arisha Rameen Bhatti, Noor Hassan, Hazrat Ali, Noor ul Huda, Habib Ur Rahman, Javeria Anwar, Anam Saqib, Mohsin Khan, Aiman Umar
description: ObjectivesThe genus Streptomyces encompasses a wide range of Gram-positive bacteria, holding significant biotechnological potential. Streptomyces species have been recognized for prolific production of multiple bioactive secondary metabolites including pigments, manifesting therapeutic potential and industrial applications. However, bioactive potential of secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces griseoincarnatus remains relatively unexplored. In this study, we isolated a S.

title: A miR-305-5p/Nerfin-1/Cyp18a1 cascade fine-tunes 20-hydroxyecdysone degradation to time pupariation in Drosophila
creator: Chan Chen, Ze Zhang, Wei Sun
description: Steroid hormone pulses provide critical temporal signals that synchronize developmental transitions, yet the mechanisms that restrain hormone clearance and preserve pulse timing remain unclear. Using Drosophila melanogaster metamorphosis, a process orchestrated by 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) pulses, this study identified Nervous fingers 1 (Nerfin-1) as a key transcriptional regulator of 20E dynamics during development.

title: Clinical validation of respiratory outcomes for a patch-based polysomnography system
creator: Holger Woehrle, Christian Viniol, Wolfgang Galetke, Georg Nilius, Christoph Schöbel, Winfried Randerath, James Leiter, Sebastian Canisius, Hartmut Schneider
description: Study objectivesThe Onera Sleep Test System (STS), the first wireless, patch-based, type II polysomnography (PSG) device designed to enable unattended sleep studies at the patient's home, has been introduced. This multicentre study validated data collected from the patch-based PSG against traditional PSG for the classification of sleep-related respiratory events.

title: Does income-related inequity exist in the utilization of home and community-based services among older adults in China? A cross-sectional study based on the China health and retirement longitudinal study 2018
creator: Songjia Zhang, Chishuang Wang, Lizheng Ge, Yuyang Zhu, Haojie Jin, Zhiming Xie, Rujia Zhang, Qingren Yang, Xiaoyi Wang, Xiangyang Zhang, Chun Chen
description: BackgroundWith escalating population aging, the significance of ensuring equitable access to elderly care services is becoming increasingly prominent. This study explored whether inequity exists in home- and community-based service (HCBS) use among older adults in China, assessed the extent of inequity, and analyzed the factors influencing the utilization of HCBSs and the resulting inequities.

title: Comprehensive species sampling reveals pervasive pseudogenization and recurrent complete loss of plastid ndh genes in the genus Cymbidium (Orchidaceae)
creator: Hai-Yao Chen, Li-Qiong Chen, Xin Yao, Zhi-Rong Zhang, Ji-Dong Ya, Xiao-Hua Jin, De-Zhu Li, Jun-Bo Yang, Wen-Bin Yu
description: BackgroundPlastome evolution in plants with diverse nutritional strategies provides unique insights into genomic-level adaptive processes. The genus Cymbidium (Orchidaceae), characterized by its heterogeneous life forms and transitions toward mycoheterotrophy, serves as an exemplary natural system for investigating chronospatial dynamics between ecological adaptation and plastomic evolutionary trajectories.

title: Neurogenic diarrhoea after superior mesenteric artery divestment or resection for pancreatic adenocarcinoma following preoperative chemotherapy: international multicentre retrospective study
creator: Thomas F Stoop, Chiara Croce, Hiroyuki Ishida, Mahsoem Ali, Ammar A Javed, Asif Halimi, Atsushi Oba, Bas Groot Koerkamp, Carl-Stephan Leonhardt, Cornelius A Thiels, Elena Rangelova, Ernesto Sparrelid, Ira Sotirova, Jennifer L Leiting, Jun Tauchi, Kosuke Kobayashi, Marit Klos, Lysanne P M Beuk, Luana
description: BackgroundThe increased use of superior mesenteric artery (SMA) divestment has been a driver behind the increased resection rate for locally advanced pancreatic cancer following preoperative therapy. This has also resulted in an increase in the rate of postoperative neurogenic diarrhoea, but knowledge about postoperative neurogenic diarrhoea is lacking.

title: BV100 (rifabutin IV) drug interaction studies in healthy subjects with index CYP450 3A probes midazolam and itraconazole
creator: Pierre Delique, Christian Kemmer, Lisa Husband, Géza Lakner, Jürgen Jäger, Françoise Jung, Andrew F Shorr, Glenn E Dale
description: BackgroundBV100 is a novel intravenous (IV) formulation of rifabutin under development for the treatment of serious Acinetobacter baumannii infections. The primary objectives of these studies were to assess potential pharmacokinetic interactions between BV100 and two index cytochrome P450 3A enzymes (CYP3A) probes, midazolam (substrate) and itraconazole (inhibitor), and to evaluate BV100’s safety profile.

title: Analytical validation, reference interval determination, and diagnostic performance of plasma symmetric dimethylarginine in cattle
creator: Charly De Campos, Inês de Brito Neves Barroca, Zahida Baydoun, Théo Chenal, Manon Gonçalves-Brandão, François Schelcher, Catherine Trumel
description: BackgroundThe efficacy of serum urea and creatinine concentrations in the diagnosis of kidney disease in cattle is limited because of their low sensitivity and specificity. Serum symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) concentration is correlated with glomerular filtration rate and has been reported to be useful for the diagnosis of kidney disease in other species.

title: Prospective Phase II Trial of Biweekly Gemcitabine Plus Nab‐Paclitaxel as First‐Line Therapy in Patients Aged 75 Years and Older With Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer
creator: Kenji Ikezawa, Toshihiro Imai, Ryoji Takada, Takuo Yamai, Nobuyasu Fukutake, Makiko Urabe, Yugo Kai, Kaori Mukai, Tasuku Nakabori, Kazuyoshi Ohkawa
description: BackgroundAlthough older adults (≥ 75 years) constitute a large proportion of patients with unresectable pancreatic cancer (PC), they remain underrepresented in clinical trials. Biweekly gemcitabine plus nab‐paclitaxel (GnP) has been evaluated in retrospective studies as an alternative dosing schedule, whereas prospective evidence remains limited.

title: Analysis of a household-scale model for the invasion of Wolbachia into a resident mosquito population
creator: Abby Barlow, Sarah Penington, Ben Adams
description: In areas infested with Aedes aegypti mosquitoes it may be possible to control dengue, and some other vector-borne diseases, by introducing Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes into the wildtype population. Thus far, empirical and theoretical studies of Wolbachia release have tended to focus on the dynamics at the community scale. However, Ae.

title: Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging parameters predict new-onset symptoms of heart failure in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
creator: Danuzia S da Silva, Vanessa Karlinski Vizentin, Iuri Ferreira Felix, Maren Maanja, Simmy A Lahori, Kalyan S Pasupathy, Steve R Ommen, Jeffrey B Geske, John R Giudicessi, Philip A Araoz, Michael J Ackerman, Adelaide M Arruda-Olson, J Martijn Bos
description: BackgroundHypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a heritable cardiac disorder characterized by increased left ventricular (LV) wall thickness, often leading to heart failure (HF). The role of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging in predicting new onset of HF symptoms in patients with HCM remains unknown. This study aimed to identify CMR predictors of new-onset HF symptoms in individuals with HCM.

title: Exploratory single‐nucleus multiomics analysis of myeloid cell states associated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy response in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
creator: Mercy Ojetunde, Li Ma, Hillary G Goodney, Alyson M Stevens, Alan Mizener, Emidio E Pistilli, Sascha Ott, Kawther Abdilleh, Barbara Szomolay, Gangqing Hu, Timothy D Eubank, Brian A Boone
description: BackgroundPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) continues to be one of the most lethal human malignancies, with the vast majority of patients ineligible for immunotherapy. Tumour‐associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the PDAC tumour microenvironment (TME), yet their transcriptional and epigenomic heterogeneity in the context of chemotherapy response is poorly understood.

title: Severe relapse of Evans syndrome in an adult patient with treatment resistance and fatal outcome: A case report
creator: Amr R Saleh, Ziad W Elmezayen, Alaa Zayed, Eman Ali Elhawary
description: Evans syndrome is an uncommon autoimmune disorder characterized by autoimmune hemolytic anemia and immune thrombocytopenia. It can follow a relapsing course in adults and may be challenging to treat. A woman in her 50s, diagnosed with Evans syndrome 2 years ago and on 10 mg prednisolone once daily, presented with worsening symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and abnormal uterine bleeding.

title: The Indian Smell Identification Test for Parkinson’s Disease: Limitations of Binary Scoring and Proposal of a Modified Graded Approach
creator: Tarunya Nagaraj, Shweta Prasad, Shubha GS Bhat, Mahima Bhardwaj, DK Samartha, Pooja Mailankody, Rohan R Mahale, Nitish Kamble, Vikram V Holla, Ravi Yadav, Pramod K Pal
description: Background and Objectives:Olfactory dysfunction is a common nonmotor symptom and prodromal marker of Parkinson’s disease (PD). Despite its early occurrence, hyposmia is frequently underrecognized, emphasizing the need for objective, culturally appropriate tools. The Indian smell identification test (INSIT) is widely used but relies on binary scoring, which may underestimate residual olfactory function.

title: Prioritising modifiable risk factors for self-management of urinary incontinence in older men: integrating expert consensus with patient readiness
creator: Olawunmi Olagundoye, Thomas F Monaghan, William Gibson, Adrian Wagg
description: BackgroundUrinary incontinence (UI) affects up to one-third of men aged ≥65 years, yet evidence to guide the selection of targets for self-management interventions remains limited. Although many contributing risk factors are potentially modifiable, little is known about which are considered clinically important by experts and are also viewed by older men as feasible and worthwhile to address.

title: Longitudinal human transcriptomic and spatial gene profiling at the incisional edge during long surgical procedures
creator: Matthew R Sapio, Evelyn Li, Anthony F Domenichiello, Taichi Goto, Dragan Maric, Allison P Manalo, Tracy S Williams, Saber Tadros, Jonathan M Hernandez, David S Schrump, Jeremy L Davis, Andrew M Blakely, Michael J Iadarola, Andrew J Mannes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Post-surgical pain remains a widespread problem reducing quality of life. The present study investigates the initial molecular changes underlying nociceptive sensitization through longitudinal, temporal sampling at the surgical wound edge. Using RNA-Seq and multiplex fluorescence in situ hybridization, we examined the most significant genes induced by tissue injury including those coding for the secreted factors interleukin 6, oncostatin M and leukemia inhibitory factor, and localized these induction events to several cutaneous structures including the epidermis, vascular endothelia, hair follicles, and sweat glands.

title: Retraction Note: Optimizing credit card fraud detection with random forests and SMOTE
creator: P. Sundaravadivel, R. Augustian Isaac, D. Elangovan, D. KrishnaRaj, V. V. Lokesh Rahul, R. Raja
description: n the description provided in the Article the source of the data appears unclear. In addition, there are concerns about the inclusion of non-existent references. The Authors did not provide the underlying raw data and their response to the Editors did not resolve the concerns. The Editors have therefore lost confidence in the data, results, and conclusions of this Article.

title: Impact of Clinicopathological and Institutional Factors on the Clinical Courses of Patients With Localized Prostate Cancer Initially Managed by Active Surveillance: An Analysis of Nationwide Real‐World Data From Japan
creator: Mizuki Onozawa, Masaki Shiota, Taketo Kawai, Shinichi Sakamoto, Yoshiyuki Yamamoto, Satoru Taguchi, Yasuhide Kitagawa, Tohru Nakagawa, Shiro Hinotsu, Jun Miyazaki, Haruki Kume, Japan Study Group of Prostate Cancer (J‐CaP)
description: ObjectivesTo investigate active surveillance (AS) continuation rates and associated clinical and institutional factors in Japanese patients with localized prostate cancer.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 989 patients with localized prostate cancer from 92 institutions who initiated AS between 2016 and 2018. Institutions were categorized into three groups based on AS uptake for low‐risk disease. Discontinuation triggers and subsequent treatments were examined.

title: Laryngeal leiomyosarcoma: A rare case report and literature review
creator: Bolat Shalabaev, Svetlana Kurash, Aibar Nurzhanov, Dulat Serikbaiuly, Bayram Kochiev, Almira Manatova, Zhandos Burkitbayev, Zhuldyz Kuanysh
description: Background: Laryngeal leiomyosarcoma (LLMS) is an exceptionally rare malignant tumor, accounting for less than 1 % of all laryngeal cancers, which are predominantly epithelial in origin. Since the first description in 1939, fewer than 70 cases have been reported worldwide.

title: Associations between daily physical activity timing and sleep efficiency revealed by explainable machine learning
creator: Jihee Choe, Yujin Oh, Chanwoo Park, Young Kim, Changwon Wang, Se Dong Min
description: Sleep deprivation has a significant impact on health and quality of life, with approximately 30% of adults worldwide suffering from insomnia. Physical activity has been recognized as a promising non-pharmacological intervention method, but the daily association between sleep and physical activity has not been clarified because key factors such as circadian rhythms and activity times have not been considered.

title: Prophylactic three-dimensional funnel mesh for prevention of parastomal hernia: propensity-score-matched cohort study
creator: Jacques-Emmanuel Saadoun, Eleftherios Gialamas, Alexandre Balaphas, Cécile de Chaisemartin, Hélène Meillat, Bernard Lelong, Christian Toso, Emilie Liot, Jérémy Meyer, Guillaume Meurette, Frédéric Ris
description: nce, PSH significantly impacts quality of life and remains difficult to treat, with high recurrence rates after repair. Preventive strategies are therefore essential, yet the optimal approach remains debated. Considering this problem, funnel-shaped three-dimensional (3D) meshes have emerged as a promising alternative, since Berger first described the technique2. This design stabilizes the bowel loop and reduces local tension.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Smoking Cessation Interventions Integrated Into Lung Cancer Screening
creator: Pianpian Cao, Laney Smith, Emma Tian, Lou-Anne Chichester, Elizabeth Schofield, Randi M. Williams, Rafael Meza, Benjamin A. Toll, Jamie Ostroff, Elena B. Elkin, Steven S. Fu, Stephanie R. Land, Kathryn L. Taylor, Jinani Jayasekera
description: Key PointsQuestionWhat is the cost-effectiveness of integrating smoking cessation interventions with varying intensity into lung cancer screening programs in the US?FindingsIn this economic evaluation of 2520 individuals enrolled in 4 randomized clinical trials, trial data were projected over a lifetime horizon using an established microsimulation model.

title: Taphonomic patterns of a WWI Alpine mass grave: insights from the Italian front
creator: Wiktoria Baranowska, Mauro Gobbi, Stefano Vanin, Franco Nicolis, Daniel Gaudio
description: Understanding taphonomic patterns on skeletal remains, along with associated entomological evidence, remains a critical challenge in forensic and archaeological investigations. This study examines the specific impact of an Alpine environment on a WWI mass grave of 12 Austro-Hungarian soldiers (Cima Cady, Italy).

title: Reduced cough severity and improved confidence in self-management following completion of a Virtual Physiotherapy Group Intervention for Chronic Cough: ViP-Cough
creator: Charles C. Reilly, Ellen Shiner, Sarah V. Floyd, Inge Vermeulen, Cameron Ross, Peter Cho, Caroline J. Jolley, Surinder S. Birring
description: IntroductionProlonged waiting times significantly limited access to our respiratory physiotherapy service for cough control therapy. In response, we developed a virtual physiotherapy group intervention for individuals with chronic cough (ViP-Cough) to improve accessibility. This article describes the uptake and potential benefits of this novel approach.

title: Diversity, equity, and inclusion as scientific rigor: progress during challenging times
creator: Leticia M Nogueira, Matthew F Hudson, Barbara Pistilli, Howard Hochster, Stefan Ambs, Martin R Stockler, James B Yu, Eduardo L Franco
description: ts are better equipped to identify blind spots, interrogate and challenge dominant assumptions, and produce innovative and impactful knowledge.1-4 We remain committed to these principles. Over the past several years, the Journal of the National Cancer Institute (JNCI), JNCI Cancer Spectrum, and JNCI Monographs undertook a series of deliberate efforts to advance DEI across editorial processes and scholarly output.

title: A novel single-cell level evaluation method for corneal endothelial cell function
creator: Dongfang Li, Zongyi Li, Haoyun Duan, Xinhang Wang, Zhan Lin, Kun Dai, Quan Qi, Yanling Dong, Ping Lin, Wenjie Su, Shuting Wang, Xiangyue Hu, Xiaojing Pan, Xiaomin Liu, Qingjun Zhou, Lixin Xie
description: Approximately 10 million people worldwide suffer from corneal diseases, with endothelial dysfunction being a leading cause of blindness. Current morphological assessments lack sensitivity for detecting early corneal endothelial abnormalities. Here, we present a novel diagnostic framework that evaluates endothelial cell function at the single-cell level by analyzing morphological alterations.

title: Diabetes mellitus and abdominal aortic aneurysm growth: Clinical evidence and mechanistic insights
creator: Margaret Dimova, Bistra Boneva, Boris Ilchev
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDiabetes mellitus (DM) has paradoxically been associated with slower abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) growth, despite its adverse vascular profile.MethodsWe present a focused synthesis of contemporary longitudinal cohort studies reporting AAA growth rates according to diabetes status and metformin exposure.ResultsAcross six independent cohorts, patients with diabetes consistently exhibited slower aneurysm expansion compared with patients without diabetes, with reported differences of approximately 0.5–1.5 mm/year.

title: Combining AI Structure Prediction and Integrative Modeling for Nanobody-Antigen Complexes
creator: Miguel Sánchez-Marín, Marco Giulini, Alexandre M.J.J. Bonvin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Nanobodies exhibit antigen-binding affinities of the same order as those of antibodies, which, along with their small size and unique structural characteristics, makes them well-suited for therapeutic and diagnostic applications. The lack of coevolutionary signals in nanobody-antigen complexes, together with the broad complementarity determining region 3 loop (CDR3) conformational space, poses a challenge for predicting the 3D structure of those complexes with computational modeling and artificial intelligence-based methods. In this context, physics-based information-driven docking can provide an alternative solution.

title: Investigation of the loading and release behavior of paracetamol, mesalazine, and carbamazepine utilizing Cu-and Zn(BDC) MOFs
creator: Golnaz Zahabi, Roya Nayebi, Abdollah Fallah Shojaei
description: In this work, Cu(BDC) and Zn(BDC) metal organic frameworks were synthesized using an ultrafast ultrasound-assisted method at room temperature for loading and releasing the drugs paracetamol, carbamazepine, and mesalazine. The synthesized MOFs were characterized and identified using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, SEM, and UV-Vis analyses, and the characterization data were complemented by BET and EDX surface area measurements.

title: A Framework for Building an Inclusive Quality Program in a Pediatric Heart Center
creator: Judson A. Moore, Jennifer Marietta, Adam L. Ware, David K. Bailly, Kevin Hummel, Aaron W. Eckhauser, Chuck G. Pribble, Melissa M. Winder, Tina Wadhwa, Emilee T. Glenn, Ashlee Gardner, Megan Wichser, Haley Francione, Carly Heyrend, Chelsea Buckalew, Bethany Marullo, Venu Amula, Adil Husain, Antonio G
description: Introduction:Pediatric heart centers have advanced quality improvement (QI) work through registries and collaboratives, improving benchmarking and shared learning. However, institutions must also build internal, sustainable QI programs tailored to local needs. We outlined our experience in developing an inclusive QI program that provides a structured framework to drive continuous improvement.

title: Automated and manual model creation workflows are equally reliable for virtual mechanical testing of ovine bone and fracture healing
creator: Mehran Bahrami, Alireza Ariyanfar, Karina Klein, Brigitte von Rechenberg, Salim Darwiche, Hannah L. Dailey
description: Virtual mechanical testing on image-based bone models (digital twins) provides subject-specific insights about the mechanical behavior of a bone during fracture healing. However, the established workflows for these tests are limited by reliance on commercial software and time-consuming manual procedures needed to create the digital twins.

title: PockLigGPT: Pocket-Sequence-Conditioned Molecular Generation with GPTs and RL
creator: Pablo Varas Pardo, Guillermo Marcos-Ayuso, Eugenia Ulzurrun, David Ríos Insua, Nuria E. Campillo
description: De novo drug design aims to generate molecules targeting specific protein pockets while retaining chemical plausibility and drug-like properties. Recent 3D structure-based generative methods explicitly model pocket-ligand geometry, but this does not always translate into chemically realistic or practically usable candidate molecules. Molecular language models provide a complementary sequence-based alternative.

title: Antimutagenic effects of a tea made from Actinidia arguta, sarunashi in Japanese, and its inhibitory effects on the formation of aberrant crypt foci induced by 1,2-dimethylhydrazine in mice
creator: Yusuke Saiki, Naoko Miyake, Sakae Arimoto-Kobayashi
description: We previously determined the antimutagenic activity of the juice of Actinidia arguta (hereafter referred to as sarunashi-juice) using the Ames test. The anticarcinogenic effect of sarunashi-juice was observed in lung and skin tumorigenesis in mice. We hypothesized that tea prepared from the leaves and twigs of A. arguta (hereafter referred to as sarunashi-tea) might also have antimutagenic and anticarcinogenic properties.

title: Microbialite Diversity and Ocean Redox Geochemistry of the Late Tonian Callison Lake Formation
creator: Charlotte Spruzen, Malcolm W. Wallace, Maxwell A. Lechte, Ashleigh V. S. Hood, Brennan O'Connell, Galen P. Halverson
description: Microbialites provide a unique insight into ancient microbial processes and environments, but trends in the diversity of unlaminated microbialites remain poorly understood. The ca. 745 Ma Callison Lake Formation in the Yukon (northwest Canada) features a range of microbialites which are diverse at both the mesoscale and microscale.

title: Laser-Induced Thermal Decomposition of Uranium Single-Source Precursors to Form Uranium Ceramics
creator: Sheridon N. Kelly, Andrew J. Swift, Maryline G. Ferrier, Aiden A. Martin, Jason R. Jeffries, John Arnold, Bradley C. Childs
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Three molecular precursors (uranium amidinate, thioamidate, and amidate) were subjected to laser-based heating to assess how laser irradiation (T > 2000 °C and rapid cooling) changes uranium material formation compared to more mild conditions in furnace heating. Simultaneous thermal analysis was conducted to study mass loss and decomposition profile of the precursors under mild conditions, and suggests formation of uranium nitride, sulfide, and oxide materials.

title: Supporting meaningful public involvement and engagement in health research: a call for feedback on unsuccessful grant proposals
creator: Matthias Eberl, Sienna-Mae Yates, Sarah Peddle, Jim Fitzgibbon, Sarah Hatch
description: Funders increasingly emphasise patient and public involvement and engagement (PPIE) as an integral component of health and biomedical research. This shift reflects broader commitments to inclusivity, transparency and accountability, recognising that lived experiences enhance the relevance, feasibility and impact of research. PPIE can improve study design, recruitment and dissemination, supporting a transition from expert-led to co-created knowledge generation.

title: 血管内皮生长因子C参与脑膜淋巴管介导β淀粉样蛋白清除的研究进展
creator: 赵勰 於, 瑶 汪, 亚楠 李, 峰 沈, 彦春 王
description:
阿尔茨海默病（AD）是一种以β淀粉样蛋白（Aβ）沉积为核心病理改变的神经退行性疾病。脑膜淋巴管是Aβ清除的重要通路，其功能障碍加速AD进展。血管内皮生长因子C（VEGF-C）通过激活血管内皮生长因子受体3及下游信号通路，协同促进淋巴管新生、增强淋巴管通透性及调节淋巴液流动，提高Aβ清除效率。遗传因素和衰老相关因素导致VEGF-C衰减进而削弱脑膜淋巴管功能，形成恶性循环。本文综述了VEGF-C调控脑膜淋巴管结构和功能促进Aβ清除的作用机制，总结了遗传和衰老通过影响VEGF-C导致脑膜淋巴管功能障碍的证据，并展望了基于VEGF-C调控脑膜淋巴管的AD个体化干预策略，以期为AD防治研究提供参考。

AD是一种以进行性认知功能障碍为主要特征的神经退行性疾病。全球AD患者数量持续攀升，预计2050年将达1.52亿［1］，疾病负担严峻。AD的病理特征包括脑内Aβ沉积、τ蛋白过度磷酸化形成神经原纤维缠结以及神经元丢失等［2］。其中，Aβ异常沉积被视为AD发病的核心机制之一，它会引发炎症反应、氧化应激和突触功能障碍，最终导致神经元死亡［3-4］。近年来，研究逐渐揭示了脑膜淋巴系统在Aβ清除过程中的作用。作为脑脊液引流的关键通路，脑膜淋巴管不仅参与中枢神经系统的免疫调节和炎症反应，还构成了脑内代谢物清除的核心结构［5］。脑膜淋巴管通过将包括Aβ在内的代谢产物转运至颈部淋巴结进行降解，有效维持了脑组织内环境稳态［6］。VEGF-C作为淋巴管新生的关键调控因子［7］，在调节脑膜淋巴管结构和功能方面的作用受到关注。

VEGF-C属于血管内皮生长因子家族成员，对淋巴管内皮细胞具有高度特异性［8-9］，其通过与淋巴管内皮细胞表面的VEGFR3结合，驱动脑膜淋巴管新生和功能维持［10-11］。在分子机制层面，VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴具有明确的级联反应：VEGF-C与VEGFR3结合可激活下游信号通路［12］，且VEGF-C的成熟和活化依赖于ADAMTS3和CCBE1介导的蛋白质水解及加工过程［13-14］；进一步激活PI3K/Akt和MEK/ERK等信号通路促进淋巴管内皮细胞增殖和迁移［12， 15］。此外，Ras/MAPK/Ets信号通路介导的p300招募及组蛋白乙酰化修饰可上调VEGFR3的转录水平［13］；而YAP/TAZ信号通路则通过维持转录因子Prospero相关同源异形框蛋白1表达，进一步支持淋巴管和淋巴静脉瓣发育及功能完整性［16］。上述机制协同保障脑膜淋巴管的结构生成和功能成熟，并通过调节收缩性及通透性促进Aβ等代谢物有效外排，从而维持中枢神经系统的免疫稳态。本文旨在系统阐述VEGF-C在脑膜淋巴管介导的Aβ清除过程中的作用机制，以期为AD的防治提供依据。

阿尔茨海默病状态下脑膜淋巴管Aβ清除功能受损

AD病理状态下脑膜淋巴管结构和功能异常

脑膜淋巴管是近年来确认的中枢神经系统外围重要淋巴网络，主要沿硬脑膜静脉窦、颅底及筛板分布，经过颅底和颈静脉孔引流至颈深淋巴结，最终回流至外周循环［17-18］。脑膜淋巴管的管壁主要由内皮细胞构成，其引流方向性与内皮细胞瓣膜样结构及淋巴瓣膜有关；淋巴管内皮细胞间黏附连接和紧密连接则参与维持管壁完整性，并调节淋巴管通透性［19］。功能上，脑膜淋巴管是“脑—颈淋巴轴”的核心枢纽，负责脑脊液吸收、代谢物清除及脑膜免疫监测，可与胶质淋巴系统协同，将代谢产物经动脉周隙从脑实质引流至颈部淋巴系统［20-22］。作为中枢神经系统与外周免疫系统的交流通道，脑膜淋巴管调节T细胞活化、免疫耐受和炎症平衡［17， 23］。研究表明，阻断脑膜淋巴引流可改变抗原呈递细胞分布，降低T细胞对中枢抗原的应答，影响小胶质细胞的反应性，提示免疫监视功能受损［23-25］；而促进脑膜淋巴管生长则可增强抗原递送和免疫监测功能，支持其在免疫稳态和代谢物清除中的重要作用［26］。

在自然衰老及AD病程中，脑膜淋巴管结构和功能完整性均呈显著下降趋势。形态学研究表明，脑膜淋巴管存在明显的区域结构异质性，其中背侧脑膜淋巴管多呈管径较小、分支较少、管腔呈不连续性结构且缺乏瓣膜［27］。功能学研究发现，AD模型小鼠脑脊液向颈深淋巴结的转运速率下降，部分脑脊液标志物在硬脑膜滞留，提示脑膜淋巴管的引流效率显著降低［28］。进一步研究表明，AD状态下脑膜淋巴管周围免疫微环境发生重构，具体表现为巨噬细胞、树突状细胞和T淋巴细胞等免疫细胞亚群比例失调，并伴有多种促炎性细胞因子（如IL-12、趋化因子CC配体2）表达增加，这种慢性炎症微环境可进一步抑制脑膜淋巴管的正常功能［17］。磁共振成像技术已实现人脑膜淋巴管结构的在体可视化，通过磁共振成像可观察到其随年龄增长出现的形态变化，这为脑膜淋巴管在AD中的临床相关性提供了直接影像学证据［18］。

脑膜淋巴管结构和功能异常导致Aβ清除受损

研究证明脑膜淋巴管功能障碍是加速Aβ积累和AD病理进展的重要因素［29］，通过结扎颈深淋巴结或选择性破坏脑膜淋巴管，APP/PS1小鼠的脑实质和脑膜中Aβ沉积显著增加，并出现神经炎症、突触蛋白丢失和认知功能下降等AD样表型［30］。即使在年轻的无认知障碍小鼠中，脑膜淋巴管损伤也能迅速引发认知功能衰退，并伴随小胶质细胞激活及脑血管基因转录组异常［27］。机制层面，脑膜淋巴管功能障碍可削弱淋巴引流，影响Aβ清除并促进其在脑内沉积；同时，淋巴引流受损会加重AD相关小胶质细胞的炎症反应，进而阻碍Aβ病理负荷清除［31］。

近年来研究表明，脑膜淋巴管并非静态通道，其结构和功能具备可干预性。例如，近红外光刺激可增强脑膜淋巴管的引流功能并改善其内皮细胞结构，减少AD模型小鼠的Aβ沉积并改善认知表现，提示调控脑膜淋巴管功能可能作为改善AD病理进程的治疗靶点［28］。长期运动能有效增加脑膜淋巴管直径和引流量，促进脑膜淋巴管可塑性，减少海马及皮层Aβ沉积，改善AD小鼠认知功能［32］。

血管内皮生长因子C可调控脑膜淋巴管结构和功能

VEGF-C是调控脑膜淋巴管结构和功能的核心信号分子，作用机制见图1。其可能通过促进淋巴管新生、增强淋巴管通透性、调节淋巴液流动等多重途径，参与脑脊液引流和脑内Aβ清除。

VEGF-C调控脑膜淋巴管结构和功能的机制示意图

Schematic diagram of the mechanism by which VEGF-C regulates meningeal lymphatic vessel structure and function

健康状态下脑膜淋巴管分布较完整，AD状态下脑膜淋巴管出现变细、稀疏等退行性改变. 以硬脑膜区域为例示意脑膜淋巴管与蛛网膜下腔脑脊液之间的溶质转运：健康状态时，淋巴管内皮细胞表面VEGFR3高表达，VEGF-C通过激活该受体维持脑膜淋巴管结构完整性和引流功能，脑脊液中Aβ等大分子代谢物可经脑膜淋巴管排出；AD病理状态时，脑膜淋巴管的管腔变窄且覆盖减少，VEGFR3表达减少，脑脊液中Aβ等大分子代谢物经脑膜淋巴管的清除效率下降，Aβ在蛛网膜下腔沉积增加. VEGF-C：血管内皮生长因子C；AD：阿尔茨海默病；VEGFR3：血管内皮生长因子受体3；Aβ：β淀粉样蛋白. 利用Figdraw绘制.

促进淋巴管新生和维持结构可塑性

VEGF-C是淋巴管生成的重要调控因子，通过作用于淋巴管内皮细胞表面的VEGFR3，激活PI3K/Akt等下游信号通路，调控淋巴管内皮细胞迁移及管腔形成，进而促进淋巴管生成［33］。在脑膜淋巴管中，VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴对其发育、结构维持及可塑性具有关键作用。阻断VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴可导致脑膜淋巴管发育受阻或成年脑膜淋巴管退化；增强VEGF-C表达可诱导脑膜淋巴管生成或扩张，并改善其覆盖范围和引流潜力［34］。而且，成年脑膜淋巴管并非静态结构，其形态和分布仍可随VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴变化而动态调整，具有一定的结构可塑性［29， 34］。研究表明，在成年小鼠中，VEGF-C缺失导致脑膜淋巴管显著退化和淋巴引流功能障碍，而VEGF-C过表达则能有效诱导脑膜淋巴管新生［34］；对老年小鼠脑部进行VEGF-C治疗能有效增加脑膜淋巴管直径、促进其新生，并增强大脑中Aβ清除能力［29］。因此，VEGF-C可能通过促进脑膜淋巴管新生和结构重塑，加快淋巴液经脑膜淋巴管流动，进而增强脑脊液及其所携带的神经毒性物质向颅外引流，促进Aβ清除。

增强淋巴管通透性

研究表明，在5xFAD转基因AD小鼠中给予VEGF-C不仅可促进脑膜淋巴管扩张和发育，增加其长度和分支点数，还可改善脑脊液中大分子物质的转运效率［31］。这一结果提示，VEGF-C可能通过增强脑膜淋巴管通透性，促进Aβ等大分子代谢物清除。其机制可能涉及两个方面。其一，VEGF-C与VEGFR3结合后可激活下游信号通路（如Akt磷酸化），诱导淋巴管内皮细胞间连接重塑，使细胞间隙增大及连接松散度增加［35-37］。这种内皮屏障功能的可逆性改变有助于Aβ等大分子代谢物穿过内皮层进入淋巴管腔，随后被转运至颈深淋巴结等外周部位清除［38］。其二，在分子层面，紧密连接蛋白5和闭锁蛋白是维持淋巴管内皮屏障完整性的关键分子，其表达水平和分布可直接影响内皮细胞通透性［39-40］。VEGF-C可通过调节这些紧密连接蛋白的表达和定位［41］来优化淋巴管内皮屏障特性，提高其对Aβ等大分子代谢物的转运能力。

调节淋巴液流动

在淋巴管的发育和成熟过程中，VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴主要作用于淋巴管内皮细胞，参与调控淋巴管内皮细胞迁移、管腔样结构形成及淋巴管生成［33］。随着淋巴管网络进一步成熟，集合淋巴管逐渐建立连续性内皮连接和管腔内瓣膜，并募集平滑肌细胞环绕管壁，从而增强管壁稳定性并维持淋巴液单向运输［42］。这一作用对于维持淋巴管结构完整性、提供必要的管壁张力以及产生规律收缩至关重要，是保障淋巴液有效向前推进的动力学基础。VEGF-C介导的淋巴管内皮细胞调控可加速淋巴引流，从而提升Aβ等代谢物从脑组织经脑膜淋巴管向外周的清除效率［43］。研究发现，在AD小鼠模型中，脑膜淋巴管功能状态可影响小胶质细胞对Aβ病理的反应及抗Aβ免疫治疗效果，VEGF-C干预后可提高Aβ清除效果［31］，其可能机制在于VEGF-C通过增强脑膜淋巴管引流功能，促进Aβ相关代谢产物由脑实质向脑膜淋巴系统转运，从而提高抗Aβ单克隆抗体介导的Aβ清除效率。

综上，VEGF-C通过促进脑膜淋巴管新生、增强淋巴管通透性以及调节淋巴液流动，构成了一个多维协同作用的网络，VEGF-C可能是改善和增强脑膜淋巴管功能、促进Aβ清除的关键分子靶点。

遗传和衰老通过影响血管内皮生长因子C导致脑膜淋巴管功能障碍

遗传因素

影响VEGF-C表达的遗传变异可通过调节脑膜淋巴管新生及功能，进而调控Aβ清除效率，并参与AD病理进程。ApoE ε4等位基因是最主要的遗传风险因素，可能通过干扰VEGF加重神经退行性疾病［44］。临床遗传学研究显示，VEGF基因启动子区－2578C/A多态性与AD及轻度认知功能损害风险相关，其中－2578位点AA基因型可增加AD发生风险，并在ApoE ε4等位基因携带者中表现出更明显的认知衰退，而且部分AD患者外周血VEGF水平升高，可能反映中枢VEGF不足及外周代偿失调，这些发现提示VEGF基因突变和ApoE ε4等位基因在促进AD进展中存在协同效应，可能通过影响VEGF-C或VEGF-A对VEGFR3的配体可用性或信号转导强度，损害脑膜淋巴管结构和功能［45］。除ApoE ε4外，直接编码通路核心元件的基因突变如基因FLT4突变可降低其编码的VEGFR3激酶活性、干扰受体成熟和膜定位，减少VEGF-C与VEGFR3结合效率及下游信号强度，影响脑膜淋巴管新生及维持，最终阻碍Aβ清除［46-47］。此外，其他影响血管稳态的基因突变则发挥间接调控作用，如NOS3基因突变可降低一氧化氮合酶活性，导致血管舒张功能障碍和神经血管单元紊乱，破坏脑内血-淋巴微环境稳态，从而削弱VEGF-C对淋巴管通透性的调控［48］。

衰老因素

衰老作为AD的核心风险因素，通过多机制协同损害脑膜淋巴管介导的Aβ清除，其中VEGF-C进行性衰减是关键环节。年龄相关性脑膜淋巴管功能障碍在AD模型中已得到证实：在年轻5xFAD小鼠中，脑膜淋巴管的结构和功能保持相对完整；而老年5xFAD小鼠则表现出显著的脑膜淋巴管功能退化［29］。这种退化与脑膜淋巴管及周围血管Aβ异常沉积密切相关［31， 49］，提示衰老微环境与Aβ神经毒性之间可能存在正反馈循环，从而加剧淋巴引流障碍［50］。在临床研究中，影像学数据进一步揭示了老年AD患者存在管径不规则、分支减少等脑膜淋巴管形态学异常及颈部淋巴结萎缩，并伴随淋巴引流效率下降［18， 51］。这种功能减退导致Aβ等毒性代谢物在脑内蓄积，加速年龄相关的神经退行性疾病进程。已有研究证实衰老过程中脑膜淋巴功能变化与大脑皮层VEGF-C表达密切相关，并提示靶向增强大脑皮层VEGF-C表达可能改善老年小鼠模型的脑膜淋巴功能障碍，这为年龄相关性中枢神经系统疾病的防治提供了新的策略［52］。

结 语

综上所述，脑膜淋巴管及其关键调控因子VEGF-C在脑内Aβ清除和AD发病机制中具有重要作用。衰老和遗传因素均可削弱VEGF-C，导致淋巴引流下降，促进Aβ沉积和神经炎症。研究表明，通过基因治疗或光刺激恢复VEGF-C活性可增强脑膜淋巴功能并促进Aβ清除，提示临床干预中适度上调VEGF-C活性具有延缓AD病理进展的潜在价值［28， 31， 53］。然而，该领域仍面临多重挑战，比如VEGF-C/VEGFR3信号轴亦参与外周淋巴管生成、血管通透性及免疫调节过程，其非靶向激活可能带来非特异性效应。因此，须开发脑膜淋巴管靶向递送和剂量可控的干预策略，明确干预时机和安全有效剂量范围，辅以更精确的成像和标记手段以实现临床监测。未来临床转化研究应考虑早期精准干预、多模态功能监测及联合治疗策略，以提高疗效并降低副作用。
