title: Brain neurovascular unit in response to intra- and extra-central nervous system cancers: implications, mechanisms, and challenges
creator: Behnaz Mirzaahmadi, Fatemeh Salahpour-Anarjan, Akbar Mousakhani, Parinaz Haddadi, Fereshteh Vaziri Nezamdoust, Reza Rahbarghazi, Mohammad Karimipour
description: The neurovascular unit (NVU) plays an important role in maintaining central nervous system (CNS) homeostasis by the dynamic control of the blood-brain barrier (BBB). An increasing amount of evidence indicates that endogenous and exogenous brain tumors can disrupt NVU integrity and function, promoting tumor progression from the brain to the blood side and vice versa.

title: Electrophilic allenes participate in polar Diels–Alder reactions: study of the reactivity and site-, regio- and stereoselectivity from a molecular electron density theory perspective
creator: Alicja Bigosińska, Dominika Gondek, Luis R. Domingo, Agnieszka Kącka-Zych
description: The reactivity and selectivities in the polar Diels–Alder (DA) reactions of two 1-sulfonyl allenes with two cyclic dienes have been studied within the Molecular Electron Density Theory (MEDT) at the M06-2X/6-311G(d,p) computational level. DFT-based reactivity indices characterize sulfonyl allenes as strong electrophiles and cyclic dienes as strong nucleophiles participating in polar reactions.

title: Green Extraction Techniques for Recovering Polyphenols From Cocoa Bean Shells for Application in Food Processing: A Systematic Review
creator: Joy Chinenye Mba, Leda Atílio Pita, Helen Obioma Agu, Chioke Amaefuna Okolo, Carmen Sílvia Fávaro‐Trindade
description: Cocoa bean shells (CBSs), a by‐product of cocoa processing, are an underutilized source of bioactive polyphenols with strong potential for functional food applications. Although several studies and reviews have investigated polyphenol extraction techniques, gaps remain in consolidating findings, optimizing extraction conditions, and understanding the synergistic effects of combined green extraction methods under comparable conditions.

title: The association between the albumin-bilirubin score and postoperative delirium and prognosis in cardiac surgery patients: a retrospective dual-center cohort study using MIMIC-IV and eICU databases
creator: Na Zhu, Xiejia Weng, Xinxin Wang, Huiyang Cai
description: BackgroundThe albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score is created to estimate liver dysfunction and then extended to more general applications. Nonetheless, the effectiveness of ALBI score in forecasting adverse outcomes in patients after cardiac surgery remains unexplored. The purpose of this study was to explore the association of the ALBI score with postoperative delirium (POD) and in-hospital mortality in patients following cardiac surgery.

title: Intermittent Drying With Heated Air and Microwaves of Dragon Fruit Foams Formulated With Different Protein Sources
creator: Matheus de Souza Cruz, Amanda Aparecida De Lima Santos, Gabriela Fonsêca Leal, Jhenifer Cristina Carvalho Santos, Guilherme Mathias Lopes, Leandro Levate Macedo, Irineu Petri Júnior, Jefferson Luiz Gomes Corrêa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to investigate red dragon fruit powder production by foam mat drying, combining a simplex centroid mixture design for foam formulation with intermittent convective drying and intermittent microwave drying. Albumin, pea protein, and soy protein were evaluated as alternative foaming agents to whey protein, and optimization was based on density, overrun, and porosity, while drainage stability was used as a qualitative screening parameter.

title: Corticosteroid Receptor Modulation in the Dorsal Striatum Prevents Morphine‐Induced Place Preference and Reduction in Dopamine Transporter (DAT) Immunoreactivity in Rats
creator: Payman Raise‐Abdullahi, Fatemeh Rezamohammadi, Mehrnoush Rahmani, Abbas Ali Vafaei, Roghayeh Pakdel, Hamed Rashidipour, Ali Rashidy‐Pour
description: Stress hormones and corticosteroid signalling influence dopaminergic transmission and reward‐related behaviours. The present study investigated whether pharmacological manipulation of corticosteroid signalling within the dorsal striatum influences morphine‐induced conditioned place preference (CPP) and dopamine transporter (DAT) regulation. Male Wistar rats were implanted with bilateral intra‐dorsal striatal cannulae and subjected to the CPP paradigm.

title: Out-of-pocket expenditure for cataract surgery in rural China: a cross-sectional survey combined with hospital administrative data
creator: Junling Zhao, Jack Hennessy, Xiaochen Ma
description: BackgroundCataract is the primary cause of blindness in China and has a low surgery uptake rate where financial factors are crucial determinants. We report updated data on the financial protection of patients with cataract surgery after the integration of urban and rural medical insurance.

title: The latest Fontan paradox: when less is more (difficult)
creator: Jeremy P Moore, Thomas Paul, Susan P Etheridge
description: an population continues to grow rapidly as the operation is applied more broadly and patient survival continues to improve. Surgical advances, intentional surveillance, and expert arrhythmia management are among the factors leading to an estimated 30-year survival of over 80%, double that from 20 years ago.

title: The effect of di̇fferent preheati̇ng methods on the intrapulpal temperature of bulk-fi̇ll composi̇te resi̇ns
creator: Hilal Ateş, Merve İşcan Yapar
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of various preheating methods applied to bulk-fill composite resins on temperature changes within the pulp chamber.Materials and MethodsTen sound human molars were used. Each tooth was sectioned 2 mm apical to the cementoenamel junction, and the occlusal surface was flattened to leave a 2 mm dentin thickness.

title: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Stroke and Gut Microbiota (2010-2024)
creator: Cong Xu, Yonghong Xu, Mo Zhao, Chaowen Chen
description: ths and 89% of the DALYs were concentrated in low- and middle-income countries. 1 , 2 Recent studies have established that gut microbiota dysbiosis in stroke patients influences disease progression via the “microbiota-gut-brain axis”. This dysbiosis is characterized by a decrease in beneficial bacteria and an increase in pathogenic species, leading to the accumulation of pro-inflammatory metabolites and exacerbated neuroinflammation.

title: Acquisition‐Recruited and MOR‐Expressing Striatal dMSNs Differentially Regulate Extinction and Cue‐Induced Relapse of Alcohol Seeking
creator: Xueyi Xie, Xuehua Wang, Jun Wang
description: Relapse to alcohol use is frequently triggered by re‐exposure to alcohol‐associated cues, and extinction‐based interventions can reduce this vulnerability. However, the striatal cellular mechanisms through which extinction alters later alcohol seeking remain unclear. Using a mouse model of operant alcohol self‐administration, we examined two distinct direct‐pathway medium spiny neuron (dMSN) populations in the dorsomedial striatum.

title: AI-generated biochemistry test item parameters in MST test conditions
creator: Murat Polat, Engin Karadag
description: BackgroundThis study investigated whether ChatGPT 4o could accurately estimate the difficulty of medical assessment items by comparing its predictions with empirically-derived parameters from multistage testing simulations.MethodsUsing a hybrid simulation-validation design, the researchers had ChatGPT 4o generate 80 multiple-choice biochemistry questions with difficulty estimates (b-parameters), which were then administered via simulated multistage testing to 5,000 virtual examinees.

title: Beak height and nest structure shape avian bite force
creator: Si-Dan Lin, Xiao-Dong Rao, Wei Liang
description: Bite force is a key performance trait in vertebrates, affecting prey capture, defense, resource competition, and other ecologically important behaviors. Despite broad functional relevance, systematic studies on avian bite force remain limited across species, and the morphological indicators used to infer bite performance are often inconsistent.

title: Multimorbidity Clusters and Depressive Symptom Networks in Old Age: Evidence From China
creator: Xin Guan, Li-gang Wang, Zhen-jing Liu, Yan-kai Zhang, Xin-mei Hao, Xin-yue Wang, Lei Zhang, Ping Sun
description: Objective To identify patterns of chronic disease multimorbidity in older Chinese adults, examine variables associated with the link between multimorbidity and depression, and characterize depressive symptom network features. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study including 2,117 adults aged ≥60 years.

title: Should we include dementia diagnosis or cognitive impairment to predict home care cost? An observational study using real-world data
creator: Flurina Meier-Schwarzer, Nicole Probst-Hensch, Marc Höglinger, Matthias Schwenkglenks, Simon Wieser
description: BackgroundThe reintroduction of dementia diagnosis into Medicare Advantage risk-adjustment models suggests that the condition independently influences Medicare costs. Similarly, Switzerland is considering specific tariffs for dementia patients in long-term care. However, the question of whether including dementia diagnosis meaningfully improves predictions of home nursing care costs is still under debate.

title: Delayed Diagnosis of Narcolepsy: Family History and Clinical Features as Predictive Factors
creator: Eun Hye Lee, Tae-Won Kim, Young-Chan Kim, Su-Hyung Kim, Yoo Hyun Um, Ho Jun Seo, Jong-Hyun Jeong, Seung Chul Hong
description: Objective Narcolepsy often begins in adolescence, yet diagnosis is frequently delayed. This study aimed to identify factors associated with delayed diagnosis of narcolepsy, defined as more than 1 year between symptom onset and diagnosis, focusing on age at onset, clinical symptoms, and family history. Methods We recruited 235 patients with clinically diagnosed narcolepsy from St.Vincent’s Hospital in South Korea.

title: Regeneration of the pulp-dentin complex in mature teeth using autologous demineralized dentin matrix and dental pulp stem cells: two case reports
creator: Misako Nakashima, Noriaki Yoshihashi, Hiroyuki Tanaka, Koichiro Iohara
description: BackgroundRegenerating the true pulp–dentin complex in mature teeth with necrotic pulps or apical lesions remains challenging, and consistent clinical evidence of dentin bridge formation is limited. This report describes two adult cases treated with regenerative endodontic therapy (RET) using autologous dental pulp stem cells (DPSCs) and demineralized dentin matrix (DDM).

title: Utility and clinical relevance of multiplex PCR panels for diagnosis of central nervous system infections
creator: Merve Gürler, Çisem Karaoğlu, Ebru Evren Yurtcu, Ebru Us, Zeynep Ceren Karahan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and objectivesMultiplex molecular panels for meningitis and encephalitis (M&E) allow rapid detection of multiple pathogens directly from cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples. Although their use is expanding, real-world data on their diagnostic yield and clinical relevance remain limited.

title: The process of nurses’ confrontation with ethical conflicts in home care: a grounded theory study
creator: Mostafa Gholami, Tahereh Najafi Ghezeljeh, Forough Rafii, Soodabeh Joolaee
description: BackgroundEthical conflicts (ECs) are an inseparable part of nursing care, particularly home care (HC). Nurses’ inability to effectively manage ECs may lead to occupational stress, job burnout, and low patient care quality. Despite various studies on ECs, there is limited research regarding the process of nurses’ confrontation with them in HC settings.

title: The Human Subiculum and Its Role in Spatiotemporal Memory and Mental Imagery
creator: Hye Ja Kang, Maria Jieun Hwang, Ji Sun Kim, Ji Yeon Kim, Marie‐Agathe Crampon de Place, Sang Ah Lee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Traditionally viewed as a mere relay station of the hippocampal formation, the subiculum is emerging as a computational hub of the medial temporal lobe, essential for multiplexed neural representations guiding behavior. While foundational animal research has revealed that its sophisticated cytoarchitecture allows for conjunctive coding of spatiotemporal information, our understanding of how such neural properties translate to human cognitive function remains incomplete.

title: Diagnostic challenges in isolated cardiac sarcoidosis
creator: Gregorio Tersalvi, Valentina A Rossi, Moritz Hundertmark, Vittorio Beltrani, Felicitas Escher, Katharina Wörgötter, Stephan Dobner, Felicia C Thianich, Giorgio Treglia, Heinz-Peter Schultheiss, Kurt Huber, Michele Martinelli, Gerhard Pölzl, Andrew N Rosenbaum, Omar F AbouEzzeddine, Martin R Grübler
description: Isolated cardiac sarcoidosis (iCS), defined by granulomatous inflammation limited to the myocardium, represents the most diagnostically challenging and prognostically adverse form of sarcoidosis. As it is fundamentally a diagnosis of exclusion, iCS diagnosis relies on the absence of extracardiac sarcoid and the integration of multimodality imaging, endomyocardial biopsy, and molecular testing, each with inherent limitations.

title: From accuracy to robustness: a comparative study of five advanced large language models on the Chinese dental licensing examination
creator: Jiarui Zhang, Pascal Ubuzima, Gaoyang Huang, En-Hsuan Lee, Yuting Wang, Huifang Xu, Lei Xia, Tingting Wu
description: BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable promise in various domains, including dentistry. This study aimed to evaluate five advanced LLMs (DeepSeek-R1, GPT-4o, OpenAI o3, GPT-5 Thinking, and Gemini 2.5 Pro) in the context of the Chinese Dental Licensing Examination (CDLE) to explore their potential in dental education and practice.

title: Sequence-directed covalent protein–RNA linkages in a single step using engineered HUH-tags
creator: Adam T Smiley, Calvin J Thoma, Natalia S Babilonia-Díaz, August J Krueger, Andrew C D Lemmex, Aspen J Hughes, Matthew R Pawlak, Kassidy J Tompkins, Robert P Connacher, Hideki Aihara, Wendy R Gordon
description: Replication-initiating HUH-endonucleases (reps) are enzymes that form covalent bonds with single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) in a sequence-specific manner to initiate rolling circle replication in plasmids and viruses. These nucleases have been co-opted for use in biotechnology as sequence-directed protein–ssDNA bioconjugation fusion partners dubbed ‘HUH-tags’.

title: Postburn Downregulation of miR‐148a‐3p and Its Regulatory Mechanism in Hypertrophic Scar Formation
creator: Yanhua Lu, Meng Yu, Jinghe Zhou, Yang Yang
description: BackgroundBurn injuries represent a common form of trauma, and their healing process poses a significant clinical challenge, frequently complicated by aberrant scarring. Recent studies have found that miR‐148a‐3p is an important regulator involved in the process of tissue fibrosis, but the specific mechanism of action of miR‐148a‐3p in burn wound repair still needs to be elucidated.

title: Exploring the role of high-fidelity simulation for pre-foundation assistantship students to improve preparedness for practice
creator: Amber Jennifer Sara Moore, Kallpana Dhas, Dilroshini Karunaratne, Krishna Dasigan, Ailie Brennan-Davies, Ankita Sahni, James Patrick, Lisa Saleh Rasool, Syeda Hridi, Sef Carter, Shiras Patel, Lianne Fakes, Mary Kelada, Ammar Shohayeb, Ana Baptista, Brent Bartholomew
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn the UK, new medical graduates frequently feel underprepared in managing acutely unwell patients. Clinical experiential learning gained, can be opportunistic and variable. Simulation-based medical education (SBME) has previously been shown to improve preparedness for practice.

title: Prognostic Value of the Eosinophil-to-Neutrophil Ratio for In-Hospital Mortality in Patients Hospitalized with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
creator: Hong-Joon Shin, Sung-Chul Lim
description: Inflammatory biomarkers reflecting acute immune responses may aid prognostic stratification in patients hospitalized with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). The eosinophil–neutrophil ratio (ENR) integrates two key inflammatory cell populations; however, its prognostic value in the acute exacerbation of COPD has not been fully established.

title: Nonlinear inverse association between hemoglobin-to-red cell distribution width ratio and short- and long-term mortality in patients with cardiac arrest: A retrospective cohort study based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database
creator: Li Zhang, Xiangxin Liao, Jia Huang, Zhaohui Zhang, Shuhan Cai, Lu Li, Zhiyong Peng, Gaosheng Zhou
description: ObjectiveCardiac arrest is a life-threatening condition associated with high mortality. This study aimed to investigate the association between the hemoglobin-to-red cell distribution width ratio (HRR) measured within 24 h of admission and 28-, 90-, and 180-day all-cause mortality in patients with cardiac arrest and evaluate its potential early prognostic value.

title: Using microwave ablation in combination with curettage and reconstruction with a vascularized iliac bone graft guided by a three-dimensional printed model for the treatment of a grade III talar giant cell tumor: a case report
creator: ZhaoHui Pan, YuXiang Zhao, XingHua Ye, JianBo Wang, Pingping Jiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundJuxta-articular giant cell tumors in the talus are very rare and pose a special problem for reconstruction after aggressive tumor curettage. Currently, vascularized iliac bone graft (VIBG) has proven to improve the outcome of partial talus defect, however, technical difficulty occurs when both the three-dimensional fitting for a large cavity and structural support to the articular surface in the talus are needed.

title: Analysis of experimental conditions for alkali activation of mining tailings based on literature data
creator: Lucimara Bragagnolo, Pedro Domingos Marques Prietto, Eduardo Pavan Korf
description: The growing focus on utilizing mining waste in construction, driven by environmental concerns, underscores its potential significance as global annual tailing production surpasses 7 billion tons. Alkaline activation of mining waste emerges as a promising approach, providing a sustainable alternative for creating value-added materials. Despite numerous studies on this subject, finding optimal ranges of values for process variables remains challenging.

title: The FN400 Tracks the Frequency of Task‐Irrelevant Distractors in the Environment
creator: Seth A Marx, Geoffrey F Woodman
description: The frontal N400 (FN400) is an event‐related potential (ERP) typically observed approximately 300–500 ms post‐stimulus and characterized by less negative (more positive) amplitudes for previously encountered stimuli relative to novel stimuli. Here we sought to determine what other statistics of the environment the FN400 might track.

title: 486. A case of prolonged delirium after the application of electroconvulsive therapy in the treatment of recurrent depressive disorder
creator: M Pantić, M Drašković Edisvog, G Mihajlović, M Jovanović
description: BackgroundElectroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an effective but underutilized treatment for depression that does not respond to antidepressants. Mild to moderate cognitive impairment is a common side effect, but usually resolves within a few hours.Aims & ObjectivesThe main goal is a description of a patient who developed delirium after the sixth application of ECT.MethodUsing ECT for treatment for reccurent depression.

title: Mortality risk due to non-optimum temperatures by cause of death, age, and sex: a multi-country time-series study
creator: Bo Wen, Yao Wu, Rongbin Xu, Pei Yu, Yanming Liu, Wenhua Yu, Tingting Ye, Wenzhong Huang, Zhengyu Yang, Yiwen Zhang, Zhihu Xu, Shuang Zhou, Yuxi Zhang, Ke Ju, Simon Hales, Eric Lavigne, Paulo Hilario Nascimento Saldiva, Micheline de Sousa Zanotti Stagliorio Coelho, Patricia Matus, Xerxes Tesoro Sepos
description: SummaryBackgroundNon-optimum temperatures have been linked to increased mortality, but the cause-, age-, and sex-specific impacts remain largely unclear. This study investigates the temperature–mortality relationships for nine causes of death across multiple countries/territories and explores subgroup differences by sex and age.

title: Perceived benefits of diet, physical activity, alcohol intake and smoking among cancer survivors: a cross-sectional study
creator: Rachel Drbohlav Ollerton, Nadine Bol, Gwenn Beets, Frans Folkvord, Emiel Krahmer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundA healthy lifestyle can have various health benefits for cancer survivors, including positive effects for their general health and cancer-specific outcomes. In general, cancer survivors adhere more to smoking and alcohol recommendations, compared to diet and physical activity recommendations.MethodsTo better understand the differences in benefit perceptions among the four health behaviours, we conducted a cross-sectional study among 197 Dutch survivors with various cancer types.ResultsWe found a positive association between perceiving benefits and engaging in respective health behaviours.

title: 249. A head-to-head comparison of two biologically-based subtyping solutions for major depressive disorder
creator: K Dunlop
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous psychiatric syndrome, and many patients do not respond fully to an initial trial of a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), the most prescribed first-line antidepressant class. The neurobiological basis of heterogeneity in SSRI responses is poorly understood, and conventional approaches to assessing treatment response typically do not differentiate between improvements in anhedonia, mood, insomnia, and other symptom domains, which vary across individuals.

title: 636. Plasma and cerebrospinal fluid neurofilament light chain in the differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorders: a systematic review
creator: I Mangas Palma, J Paupério, L Ferreira, R Moreira
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundDistinguishing neurodegenerative disorders from primary psychiatric conditions remains a major clinical challenge, particularly in early or atypical presentations. Neurodegenerative disorders may present with prominent psychiatric symptoms, leading to substantial clinical overlap with primary psychiatric conditions and frequent diagnostic delay. Reliance on symptom-based assessment alone is therefore insufficient in clinically ambiguous cases, underscoring the need for objective biomarkers to support differential diagnosis.Neurofilament light chain (NfL) is a well-established marker of neuroaxonal injury and neurodegeneration.

title: Neonatal respiratory care in Vietnam: surfactant use and clinical practices in a large neonatal intensive care unit
creator: Hien Vu, Mårten Larsson, Linh Thi Nguyen, Thanh Phuong Thi Tran, Phuong Thu Thi Pham, Toan K Nguyen, Linus Olson, Anh Duy Nguyen, Thomas Drevhammar, Tobias Alfvén, Nicolas J Pejovic, Susanna Myrnerts Höök
description: BackgroundNeonatal mortality remains a significant health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income settings, where respiratory distress is a major contributor to mortality. Characterizations of respiratory care practices in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), in lower-middle-income contexts in south-east Asia, are notably sparse in the literature.

title: Quality of life and outcomes of patients operated on for glioblastoma
creator: Haman Nassourou Oumarou, Foka Tacsing Bolivers Kahn, Anu Ronaldo Fonju, Ghislain Guea Ngbwa, Djientcheu Vincent De Paul
description: Background: Glioblastoma is the most common and aggressive primary malignant brain tumor in adults, with a poor prognosis despite multimodal treatment. This study aimed to describe the diagnostic aspects, therapeutic strategies, quality of life (QoL), and outcomes of patients operated on for glioblastoma at the Yaoundé General Hospital.Methods: This was a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Yaoundé General Hospital.

title: 699. Etiology of PUI: biopsychosocial mechanisms
creator: M Brand, A Brandtner, J Solly, N A Fineberg, C FOR2974, C Bootstrap
description: BackgroundSince Problematic Usage of the Internet (PUI) is a growing public health concern, identifying mechanisms that contribute to its development and maintenance is of utter importance. Mounting evidence suggests that there are at least two main mechanistic drivers which contribute to the development and maintenance of symptoms of PUI, namely difficulties in affect regulation and difficulties in inhibitory control.

title: Comorbidity of internet gaming disorder and anxiety in first-year Chinese university students: the mediating role of behavioral inhibition and activation systems
creator: Jie Chen, Zhenzhen Zhang, Siwen Fu, Biyu Wen, Zeming Chen, Xiaochun Wang
description: BackgroundInternet gaming disorder (IGD) and anxiety frequently co-occur among young adults and represent an increasing mental health concern in China. Nevertheless, the psychological network underlying this comorbidity and the identification of potential intervention targets remain poorly understood.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study of 605 Chinese university freshmen to investigate the association between internet gaming disorder (IGD), anxiety.

title: Gut or Vein? Enteral Nutrition Versus Total Parenteral Nutrition in Acute Pancreatitis: A Systematic Review
creator: Harnoor Kaur, Archit Sharma, Palangutde Katherine Dimowo, Akshay Rajeev, Sabah Shakeel Shaikh, Lubna Mohammed
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acute pancreatitis is a common inflammatory condition with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients who progress to moderately severe or severe disease. Nutritional support is an essential aspect of management, although the optimal route of nutrition remains debated. This systematic review assessed whether enteral nutrition (EN), compared with total parenteral nutrition (TPN), is associated with improved clinical outcomes in patients with acute pancreatitis.

title: TAVR for Women
creator: Dritan Useini
description: diovascular trials, including coronary artery bypass grafting and percutaneous coronary intervention studies, where female participation often remains below 20%.2 In contrast, women constitute approximately half of patients enrolled in major TAVR trials,3 creating a unique opportunity to generate robust evidence in a population historically underrepresented in cardiovascular research.

title: Remimazolam tosylate vs. propofol: effects on anesthetic efficacy and renal function in living donor kidney transplantation
creator: Jiaxin Wu, Wendong Lin, Haiying Kong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundRemimazolam Tosylate (RT) is an ultrashort-acting benzodiazepine with organ-independent metabolism, suitable for patients with renal impairment. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of RT in living donor kidney transplantation.MethodsEighty-six patients with uremia who underwent living donor kidney transplantation from May 2024 to October 2024 were randomized into the RT group (group RT) or the propofol group (group P), with 43 patients per group.

title: Effectiveness of Community-Based Breast Cancer Screening Using Full-Field Digital Mammography With Digital Breast Tomosynthesis in an Urban Population in Central India: An Observational Study
creator: Shilpa Pande, Sanjay Dakhore, Deepshikha Arora, Shashikant Juvekar
description: BackgroundBreast cancer is the most common malignancy among women worldwide and remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. In India, delayed presentation and limited access to organised screening programmes contribute to poorer outcomes. Community-based screening models, combined with advanced imaging techniques, may improve early detection.

title: 241. Ectopic axonal projection from and aberrant tonotopy mapping of the auditory cortex in a schizophrenia animal model: biological implications in hallucination-like phenomena
creator: H Nawa, K Tainaka, M Tohmi
description: BackgroundAuditory hallucinations are a pathological hallmark of schizophrenia; however, the biological mechanisms underlying these symptoms remain to be elucidated. Brain-imaging studies in patients suggest that impaired frontotemporal connectivity and abnormal tonotopic organization in the auditory cortex may contribute to auditory hallucinations.

title: Microsurgical Resection and Posterior Stabilization of a Delayed Solitary Thoracic Vertebral Metastasis From a Malignant Triton Tumor: A Case Report
creator: Mars Abdaev, Yuliy Kubetsky, Evgeniy Loparev
description: Malignant triton tumor (MTT) is an aggressive variant of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) characterized by rhabdomyoblastic differentiation and an unfavorable prognosis. Spinal metastases from this tumor are exceptionally uncommon, and management strategies remain unstandardized and largely based on anecdotal evidence.

title: 436. Distinct neural correlates between suicide attempters with major depressive disorder and other psychiatric disorders: a multimodal imaging study
creator: W-S Kim, S Odkhuu, Y M Jae, Y-C Chung
description: BackgroundSuicide attempters (SA) with mild diagnoses other than major depressive disorder (MDD) are underexplored.Aims & ObjectivesThis study aimed to investigate neuroimaging abnormalities in SA with MDD (SA-MDD), SA with other psychiatric disorders (OPD) (SA-OPD), and healthy controls (HC) using MRI data. Associations between altered findings in the patient groups and anger, negative schema, or rumination were further examined.

title: A scalable post quantum secure blockchain framework with adaptive time consensus in cloud environments
creator: M. Velmurugan, M. Rajeev Kumar
description: Blockchain deployments continue to face challenges related to scalability, energy consumption, and susceptibility of classical cryptographic primitives to emerging quantum attacks. Conventional systems employing RSA or DSA signatures and consensus mechanisms such as Proof of Work (PoW) or Proof of Stake (PoS) incur substantial computational overhead and are not well suited for cloud-scale execution.

title: 344. Methylone regulates fear memory and amygdala activity: a potential treatment for posttraumatic stress disorder?
creator: C-S Lee, D Chou
description: BackgroundMethylone (3,4-methylenedioxy-N-methylcathinone) is a rapid-acting entactogen that has demonstrated significant benefits for patients with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and exhibits good tolerability in phase 1 clinical trials. Despite these promising results, its preclinical effects on fear memory regulation and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored.

title: Muscleblind-like proteins dimerize by forming disulfide bonds to regulate alternative splicing and pathogenic RNA foci formation
creator: Luke A Knudson, Adam Kosti, Ryan P Hildebrandt, Ethan Jennings, Eric X Zhou, Kathryn R Moss, Liang Shi, GiaLinh N Nguyen, Aleksandra Janusz-Kaminska, Eric T Wang, Gary J Bassell
description: Muscleblind-like (MBNL) RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) possess modular domains that mediate regulation of alternative splicing and RNA localization. In Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1, a CTG repeat expansion disorder, MBNL is sequestered into intranuclear RNA foci, impairing its function. Previous studies found that MBNL self-associates through its exon 7, but the nature of this interaction is not well understood.

title: Global, regional, and National burden of hepatitis C from 1990 to 2021 and projections until 2030
creator: Junzhu Bai, Hengliang Lv, Longhao Wang, Shumeng You, Dan Liu, Lilin Wang, Yuanyong Xu, Junfeng Lu, Wenyi Zhang
description: BackgroundBurden related to hepatitis C (HCV) has imposed severely globally. The World Health Organization has proposed a resolution to eliminate hepatitis C as a public health threat by 2030. By utilizing data from the Global Burden of Diseases (GBD) 2021, the study aims to explore the burden and prediction of diseases related to HCV globally.

title: 555. Targeting kynurenine aminotransferase III: discovery of a selective and brain-penetrant inhibitor for reducing synthesis of immune-induced kynurenic acid
creator: P Fridh, Y Gravenfors, L Schwieler, V Louvrou, M Gómez-Galán, R Caraballo, J Larsson, C Bengtsson, L Dahllund, E Woestenenk, N Nekhotiaeva, H Nordström, A Roos, A Lindqvist, E Johnson, S Erhardt
description: BackgroundKynurenic acid (KYNA) is a neuroactive metabolite produced via the kynurenine pathway. It acts as an endogenous N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) receptor antagonist and is proposed to antagonize the α7-nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR). Elevated KYNA levels are observed in several conditions, including psychotic disorders and infectious diseases, where interference with glutamatergic and dopaminergic neurotransmission contributes to psychosis and cognitive decline.

title: 853. Next-generation seizure therapy: Balancing efficacy and cognition with optimized waveforms and personalized targeting
creator: Z-D Deng
description: BackgroundElectroconvulsive therapy (ECT) remains the most effective treatment for severe, treatment-resistant depression, yet its clinical adoption is constrained by cognitive side effects stemming from widespread, non-specific E-field distribution across the brain. Present practice relies on standardized electrode placements, such as right unilateral or bitemporal, at fixed high current amplitudes, with no accommodation for individual neuroanatomy.

title: Prevalence and associated risk factors of Staphylococcus aureus nasal colonization among a cohort of immunocompromised individuals in Lagos, Nigeria
creator: Bimpe O Ogunleye, Oyewumi O Oshamika, Sharon O Akinpelu, Ayodeji S Ajayi, Paul A Akinduti, Kolawole S Oyedeji, Olalekan M Odeniyi, Olayemi O Akinnola
description: BackgroundImmunocompromised individuals are highly vulnerable to Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) infections, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, virulence, and risk factors associated with S. aureus nasal carriage among immunocompromised individuals in Lagos, Nigeria.MethodsA total of 350 participants were enrolled, including 150 HIV/AIDS cases, 50 HIV/TB co-infections, 100 diabetes cases, and 50 controls.

title: Diagnostic and management challenges of a case of N-acetylglutamate synthase deficiency in a resource-limited healthcare setting in Tanzania: a case report
creator: S Thaver, M Ebrahim, M Noorani, Zahir M Alimohamed, K Edward, F Furia, J Kwayu, Z Fidaali, Y Abdallah
description: BackgroundInborn errors of metabolism represent a significant cause of childhood morbidity and mortality. These conditions are frequently missed in low-resource settings due to their anticipated rarity and similarity of symptoms to conditions such as sepsis. We present a case of a neonate with N-acetylglutamate synthase deficiency whose diagnosis and management at our facility were complicated by limited healthcare resources.

title: Angiographic Radial Wall Strain
creator: Rui Zhang, Lei Song
description: Corresponding Author Although percutaneous coronary intervention has significantly improved outcomes for patients with coronary artery disease, the late stent-related adverse events associated with drug-eluting stents (DES) and the bleeding risks tied to dual antiplatelet therapy persist.1 These limitations sustain interest in drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty as a "leave nothing behind" strategy.

title: Effectiveness and Outcomes of Cast Immobilization in Adults With Scaphoid Waist Fractures Compared With Surgical Fixation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Safwan Alghwail, Ayman Saad, Abdulrahman K Balbaid, Abdulrahman S Alotaibi, Salman M Jathmi, Mohammed Alotaibi, Nada N Althobaiti, Saad M Al-Harthi, Mohammed Alobud, Abdullah A Adawi, Abdulaziz S Almuhaisen, Seba E Aldubian, Revan H Alomari, Ahad A Althagafi, Hoor H AlQurashi
description: The optimal management of acute, minimally displaced, or undisplaced scaphoid waist fractures is a clinical equipoise. Although cast immobilization is effective, it requires prolonged wrist restriction. Early surgical fixation aims to expedite recovery but introduces operative risks and incurs higher costs. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes contemporary, high-quality evidence comparing the effectiveness of these two management strategies.

title: 309. Cognitive correlates of functional recovery in remitted bipolar disorder
creator: S J Cho, K S Oh, J Moon
description: BackgroundCognitive impairment often persists even during remission in bipolar disorder and is recognized as a major determinant of functional recovery. However, the relative contributions of specific cognitive domains to global functioning remain unclear.Aims & ObjectivesThis study aimed to compare the predictive value of distinct cognitive domains for functional outcomes in patients with bipolar disorder during remission.

title: Patellofemoral Bipolar Osteochondral Allograft Surgery Yields Similar Short- to Mid-term Outcomes As Unipolar Surgery: A Minimum 2-year Follow-up Study
creator: Edouard Augustin, Thomas Moran, Myles Atkins, John Akinleye, Brian Cole, Kofi Acheampong, Adam B. Yanke
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:While osteochondral allograft (OCA) transplantation for tibiofemoral chondral lesions has been extensively studied, there is limited literature on outcomes following patellofemoral (PF) OCA transplantation, especially for the treatment of bipolar PF chondral lesions. This study aimed to compare graft failure rates, reoperation, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) between patients undergoing unipolar and bipolar PF OCA transplantation with a minimum follow-up of two years.Methods:A retrospective review of PF OCA transplantations between 2015-2022 at a single institution was performed.

title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission among child and adolescent contacts of people with pulmonary tuberculosis in Brazil: a multi-center prospective cohort study
creator: Luciana Sobral, María B. Arriaga, Alexandra B. Souza, Beatriz Barreto-Duarte, Beatriz S. Garcia-Rosa, Catarina D. Fernandes, Artur T. L. Queiroz, Michael S. Rocha, Aline Benjamin, Adriana S. R. Moreira, Jamile G. de Oliveira, Anna Cristina C. Carvalho, Renata Spener-Gomes, Marina C. Figueiredo, Sola
description: BackgroundChildren who are contacts of individuals with active pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) are at risk of acquiring Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection (TBI). We evaluated the determinants of TBI in child and adolescent contacts.MethodsPediatric (≤ 18 years old) close contacts of PTB patients enrolled in a multi-center Brazilian observational cohort were followed up to 6 months.

title: 282. Clozapine impairs angiogenic capacity of human endothelial progenitor cells via aryl hydrocarbon receptor–dependent mechanisms
creator: C Chen, S-W Wang
description: BackgroundClozapine, an antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, is associated with increased cardiovascular risk. Endothelial progenitor cells support vascular repair, and their dysfunction may promote atherosclerosis. How clozapine and its metabolites affect endothelial progenitor cell survival and angiogenic activity is not well defined.

title: Arthroscopic Bankart Repair with Remplissage versus Open Bankart Repair: A Multicenter Retrospective Comparative Study
creator: Fatumastar Adan, Conner Olson, Confidence Njoku Austin, Alicia Harrison, Allison Rao, Jonathan D. Harley
description: Background:The treatment algorithm for anterior shoulder instability continues to evolve. While a Bankart repair is most commonly performed arthroscopically, open Bankart repair procedures have shown good functional outcomes and have been reported to have a lower failure rate than arthroscopic techniques.

title: Physician-reported outcomes associated with collaboration between home healthcare institutions and after-hours house-call services in Japan
creator: Yu Sun, Ryota Inokuchi, Masao Iwagami, Nobuo Sakata, Ayaka Sakamoto, Nanako Tamiya
description: BackgroundIn Japan, home healthcare is a system in which physicians regularly visit patients at home to provide medical care. Additionally, the physicians are required to be available for 24-hour emergency home visits upon patient request. However, numerous single-physician home healthcare providers have been overburdened, particularly with after-hours consultations.

title: 455. Effects of adolescent cannabinoid exposure on DNA methylation in Erbb4 conditional knockout and wild-type mice
creator: Z Li, D Mukherjee, E Dempster, E Walker, R Murray, B Rico, M Di Forti
description: BackgroundAdolescent cannabis use is associated with an increased risk of psychosis, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence also pointed to genetic liability shaping individual risk of cannabis-induced psychosis. The neuregulin–ErbB4 signalling pathway, implicated in schizophrenia-related neurodevelopment, may modulate individual susceptibility to cannabis exposure.

title: Basic fibroblast growth factor preserves rabbit adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cells in serum-free culture
creator: Suryo Kuncorojakti, Ahmad Aswin, Diyantoro Diyantoro, Helen Susilowati, Ira Sari Yudaniayanti, Lina Susanti, Watchareewan Rodprasert
description: ImportanceFetal bovine serum (FBS) is widely used for mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) expansion but carries risks of contamination, batch variability, and xenogeneic exposure that can compromise reproducibility and downstream therapeutic use.ObjectiveTo develop and evaluate a rabbit adipose-derived mesenchymal stromal cell (Rab-ADMSC) serum-free medium (SFM) supplemented with growth factors that maintains key MSC characteristics.

title: Effectiveness of rimegepant in vestibular migraine: a prospective self-controlled cohort study
creator: Jinyan Shao, Jingxin Fu, Mengting Zhou, Zewei Ren, Longxiang Li, Lili Gao, Yuhui Xia, Zexian Zhao, Mengna Yang, Jiahuan He, Siyuan Xue, Guoming Wang, Jiahui He, Kaiming Liu
description: BackgroundVestibular migraine (VM) is the second most common cause of episodic vertigo worldwide, yet effective therapeutic options remain limited. This study aimed to assess the clinical effectiveness of rimegepant in patients with VM.MethodsA total of 33 VM cases were enrolled in this multicenter, prospective self-controlled cohort study, screened from an initial pool of 106 patients.

title: 411. Influence of individual personality on health functioning among medical students: a comparative study between Japan and Brazil
creator: H Fujitsuka, K Nomura, M Hiratsuka, H Akihissa Yamamoto, H Uchida, H Tani
description: BackgroundMedical students are known to have a high risk of depression due to the demanding academic environment. Although previous studies have reported associations between personality traits and anxiety/depression, cross-country comparative investigations among medical students remain limited. Japan and Brazil have contrasting sociocultural backgrounds, including differences in ethnic diversity and birth rates.

title: Trivalent fowl adenovirus vaccine (serotype-4/8b/11) provides efficient protection with long duration of immunity
creator: Dam-Hee Park, Kyeong-Cheol Min, Na-Ri Kim, Sung-Sik Yoo, Injoong Yoon, Jongseo Mo
description: ImportanceFowl adenovirus (FAdV) is a significant viral pathogen with major economic impact on the global poultry industry. Recent epidemiological studies indicate that predominant strains in Asia, including Korea, are FAdV-4 (species C), 8b (species E), and 11 (species D).ObjectiveThis study evaluated a novel trivalent inactivated FAdV vaccine containing antigens from FAdV-4, 8b, and 11.

title: 759. Addressing Clinical Trial Heterogeneity in Neuropsychiatric Long COVID Research: A Registry-Based Cross-Sectional Analysis of Pharmacotherapeutic Intervention Trial Designs
creator: N Hartman, D Ivkic, M C Dorczok, I Bozic, L Reinfried, A-C Moser, G Fugger, B Ludwig, F Buchmayer, M Spies, A Weidenauer, L Bartova, COVIKET Study Group
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLong COVID (LC) poses a considerable clinical and socioeconomic burden on affected patients and their surroundings (1-3). LC presents with diverse symptom clusters (4). One of the most prevalent is the neuropsychiatric symptom cluster. Symptoms related to this cluster are chronic fatigue, cognitive dysfunctions, symptoms related to depression and anxiety including sleep disturbances, inner tension, pain, hypersensitivity to acoustic and visual stimuli, as well as vegetative dysautonomia (5).

title: Continuous cropping drives assembly process of soil microbial community to alter keystone taxa causing challenges
creator: Fangfang Zhou, Yihong Pan, Jun Zhan, Xiaoting Li, Shunping Yu, Li Tang
description: BackgroundHealthy soil is crucial for maintaining the sustainability of soil ecosystem services and ensuring food security. The soil microbiome serves as a key indicator of soil health. However, long-term continuous monoculture significantly adversely affects the diversity and functioning of soil microbial communities, posing a serious threat to sustainable agricultural development.

title: Experimental verification of the proton range using heterogeneous animal tissue
creator: Andrew J Boria, Chia‐Ho Hua, Thomas E Merchant, Chin‐Cheng Chen
description: BackgroundProton beam therapy offers comparable tumor control to conventional photon therapy while reducing radiation‐related toxicity due to its finite range and minimal exit dose beyond the Bragg peak. However, the accuracy of proton dose delivery is highly dependent on precise knowledge of tissue stopping power along the beam path.

title: Serum Neuropeptides in Chronic Spontaneous Urticaria: Associations With Disease Activity and Clinical Phenotypes
creator: Zhenrui Shi, Xinyi Deng, Jieru Ren, Siyao Lu, Guozhen Tan
description: Neuropeptides have been implicated in chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), but clinical data remain limited. We measured serum calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), neuropeptide Y (NPY), vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP), and stem cell factor by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay in 80 patients with CSU and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls.

title: PD‐L1 Tumour‐Cell/Immune‐Cell Phenotype, Early Nodal Status and Serum Biomarkers in Locally Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Receiving Neoadjuvant Therapy: A Retrospective Cohort Study With Exploratory Survival Analysis
creator: Ningning Wang, Zehui Yun, Fangli Cao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PD‐L1 tumour‐cell (TC) and immune‐cell (IC) expression are scored separately in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) but are often collapsed into a combined positive score, potentially obscuring distinct patterns. In this retrospective, single‐centre cohort of 61 patients with locally advanced, hypopharynx‐predominant HNSCC receiving neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (n = 46) or chemotherapy alone (n = 15), we scored PD‐L1 TC% and IC% separately on pretreatment biopsies, defined four TC/IC phenotypes, classified patients by combined PD‐L1/early lymph node metastasis (ELNM) profile and related

title: 362. Possible anti-inflammatory effects of escitalopram (SSRI): reverse-translational study using human blood induced microglia-like (iMG) cells
creator: K Hiyoshi, S Kyuragi, S Inamine, M Ohgidani, T Nakao, T Kato
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPrevious research on mental disorders, including depression, has mainly been based on the hypothesis that nerves and synapses are related to mental disorders. However, recent studies have highlighted inflammation as an important disease-modifying factor in mental disorders. Animal studies have reported that antidepressants, previously thought to act on neural synapses, also have anti-inflammatory effects on microglia, which are immune cells in the brain.

title: Entanglement produced by pairs of superposed two-mode coherent and subharmonic cavity light beams
creator: Menwuyelet Melaku, Deribe Hirpo
description: We examined a two-mode coherent and subharmonic light beam within a cavity that is coupled to a two-mode vacuum reservoir through a single port mirror. Utilizing the solutions of the quantum Langevin equations, we developed Q-functions for the two-mode coherent and subharmonic cavity light beams. Subsequently, we calculated the Q-function for the superposed two-mode light beams in question.

title: How Pregnancy Affects Asthma in Korea: Risk Factors and Adherence Decline
creator: Myoung-Nam Lim, Jin-Sung Park, Jae-Woo Kwon
description: PurposePregnancy is a well-known trigger for asthma exacerbations, but risk prediction remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of pregnancy on asthma control, identify risk factors for exacerbations, and assess adherence to asthma management during and after pregnancy in Korea.

title: Delivery of lipid nanoparticles containing small interfering RNA targeting transmembrane serine protease 4 in a human gastric cancer model using nude mice
creator: Hirofumi Tazawa, Yuko Ishida, Takahisa Suzuki, Yosuke Shimizu, Hirotaka Tashiro
description: Over-expression of transmembrane serine protease 4 (TMPRSS4), which promotes epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cancer cell invasion, is associated with poor prognosis in patients with gastric cancer. This study aimed to develop a new anti-TMPRSS4 small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic strategy by engineering lipid nanoparticles (LNPs).

title: 442. Altered reward processing in animal model of autism
creator: P Amchova, S F Demirci, J Ruda-Kucerova
description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by social interaction deficits and restricted repetitive behaviors that may stem from abnormal reward processing and dopaminergic signaling in brain reward circuits (DiCarlo et al., 2023). Clinical and preclinical evidence suggests that dysregulation of mesolimbic and nigrostriatal pathways contributes both to reduced motivation for natural rewards and to enhanced stereotyped behavior (Blum et al.

title: Allergenic Characterization of Parvalbumin, Tric l 1, From Atlantic cutlassfish, Trichiurus lepturus

title: 217. SSVEP as a physiological biomarker of attentional bias and treatment response in adolescent Major Depressive Disorder
creator: S Hong, D Barrett, J-H Hu, M Rota, L Niwenhiseemo, L Kuang
description: BackgroundAttentional bias towards negative stimuli is a core mechanism in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD), yet objective biomarkers to quantify it are lacking. Steady-State Visual Evoked Potentials (SSVEP) provide a robust neural measure of attentional allocation. This study investigates SSVEP as a biomarker in adolescent MDD and its sensitivity to neuromodulation-enhanced treatment.

title: Work-Related Asthma: An Occupational Medicine Perspective
creator: Yangwoo Kim, Inah Kim, Jaechul Song
description: Work-related asthma (WRA), encompassing occupational asthma and work-exacerbated asthma, is among the most prevalent yet preventable occupational respiratory diseases, with population-based studies estimating that 10% to 25% of adult asthma cases are attributable to workplace exposure. This review examines epidemiology, causative agents, pathogenesis, clinical evaluation, management, and WRA prevention from an occupational medicine perspective, with emphasis on Korean surveillance data.

title: Fuzzy logic and deep learning approach for automated white blood cell detection and classification via multi-CNN feature fusion
creator: Taseer Ullah, Khalil Ullah, Parvez Khan, Olga Brikova, Alexander Voznesensky, Alexander Eroshkin, Ibrar Hussain
description: White blood cells (WBCs) are vital components of the human immune system, responsible for defending the body against pathogens and infections. The classification and detection of white blood cells (WBC) are indispensable for the diagnosis of hematologic diseases such as leukemia, but manual classification is time-consuming and susceptible to subjectivity.

title: 339. Brexpiprazole for emerging psychosis in an adolescent female with Asperger-type autism: a single-case clinical evaluation
creator: F Putri, K Runtuk
description: BackgroundAutism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), previously referred to as Asperger syndrome, is characterized by deficits in social communication, restricted interests, and rigid behavioral patterns. Although psychotic symptoms are not core features of ASD, adolescents with ASD are at increased risk of developing hallucinations, particularly under psychosocial stress. We present a case report using brexpiprazole in adolescents with ASD with psychotic symptoms.

title: 33. Disruption of the retinoid X receptor–PPAR-γ axis is associated with appetite hormone dysregulation and cognitive dysfunction: a cross-sectional study of adolescents with first-episode bipolar disorder
creator: M-H Chen, H-J Wu, J-W Hsu, Y-M Bai, W-C Lin
description: BackgroundThe role of the retinoid X receptor (RXR) and peroxisome proliferator–activated receptor-γ (PPAR-γ) axis in the pathophysiology of bipolar disorder (BD) remains poorly understood. The relationship of RXR–PPAR-γ axis disruption with cognitive impairment and appetite hormone dysregulation has yet to be clearly established in individuals with BD.

title: Genomic resources of Cold-adapted Mrakia yeasts and their potential biotechnological applications
creator: Seung Chul Shin, Dieu Linh Nguyen, ChanSu Jeong, Yung Mi Lee, Jun Hyuck Lee, Se Jong Han, Han-Woo Kim
description: Mrakia is a cold-adapted yeast genus commonly found in polar environments, including the Antarctic and Arctic regions. Several Mrakia genome sequences have been reported to date; however, comprehensive genomic analyses remain limited. Further, there are no reports of complete mitochondrial genome sequences for the genus Mrakia.

title: Protein modification systems as cancer biomarkers and therapeutic targets
creator: Li Gao, Yueqin He, Kexin Wang, Qin Li, Litong Nie, Lunzhi Dai
description: Protein post-translational modifications (PTMs), such as acetylation, lactylation, methylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and glycosylation, play central roles in regulating diverse cellular processes, including signal transduction, metabolic adaptation, chromatin organization, and proteostasis. In cancer, PTM networks are extensively rewired, with profound alterations in enzyme levels, protein modification landscapes, and crosstalk among different modification types.

title: 乳腺癌多基因风险综合评估在一例BRCA1突变携带者植入前胚胎选择中的应用
creator: 英辉 叶, 小玲 胡, 恺 严, 佳玲 俞, 玉琳 陈, 央云 邹, 琼 罗, 丹 张, 依敏 朱, 荷凤 黄
description: 患者不孕三年，要求辅助生殖助孕，家系乳腺癌易感基因BRCA1：c.5154G>A突变。基于UK Biobank中乳腺癌患者以及对照者遗传数据，结合亚洲人群特异性单核苷酸多态性权重构建乳腺癌多基因风险评分（PRS）313模型。经控制性卵巢刺激、胚胎培养和活检，检测胚胎BRCA1突变携带情况。结合乳腺癌PRS313评分和乳腺癌家族史信息，获得每个胚胎的乳腺癌风险综合评估结果。在上述基础上，根据胚胎染色体检测结果和胚胎发育情况选择一枚胚胎进行移植，最终妊娠并分娩一名未携带BRCA1：c.5154G>A突变活产婴儿。 世界卫生组织流行病学研究数据显示，多基因遗传病导致的死亡占总死亡数的15%~20%［1］，因此从根本上降低多基因遗传病的患病率具有重要的临床价值和深远的社会意义。多基因遗传病通常由大量遗传变异位点共同作用所致，这些变异位点单个作用效果微弱，因此对单一变异位点进行检测难以实现疾病风险评估的目的。GWAS可以用于确定大量与复杂表型相关的SNP位点。在此基础上，PRS通过整合疾病关联的多个SNP的累积效应来衡量个体性状或复杂疾病的遗传风险。 乳腺癌是一种复杂的多因素疾病，虽然目前已识别出一些中高风险易感基因（如BRCA1、BRCA2、TP53、ATM和PALB2），但这些基因在普通人群中较为罕见，在乳腺癌患者中的检出率也很低［2-3］。研究人员通过GWAS还发现了大量与乳腺癌患病风险相关的SNP，并利用PRS分层评估这些SNP对乳腺癌患病风险的影响［4-7］。Fahed等［8］研究表明，基于乳腺癌相关SNP构建的PRS对单基因变异携带者的乳腺癌风险具有修饰效应。若仅考虑个体的BRCA1/2突变携带情况，这些突变可使个体的乳腺癌风险升高4.47倍（95%CI：2.76~7.24）。当进一步结合PRS进行分析时，个体乳腺癌风险随PRS百分位数的升高而显著分层，因PRS影响的风险增幅介于1.43~16.68倍。上述结果提示，BRCA1/2突变携带者的乳腺癌风险受多基因背景（即其他常见遗传变异）精细调节。因此，综合考量乳腺癌易感单基因和SNP的联合效应对于临床精准评估个体罹患乳腺癌的风险非常必要。 基于PRS的PGT-P可通过评估胚胎遗传风险筛选用于移植的胚胎，从而降低子代患病的概率［9］。本文报道一例来自BRCA1基因阳性乳腺癌家系、需要辅助生殖技术助孕的患者，通过乳腺癌综合风险评估后进行胚胎移植，生产的子代未携带乳腺癌易感基因，供业内参考。 对象与方法 研究对象 一对夫妻因“结婚三年，未避孕未孕一年”于2023年6月就诊于浙江大学医学院附属妇产科医院生殖内分泌科拟行辅助生殖技术助孕。女方一年前因“卵巢囊肿”行“腹腔镜下右侧卵巢囊肿切除术”，术后诊断：盆腔子宫内膜异位症Ⅳ期（卵巢型、腹膜型、深部浸润型），子宫腺肌病。女方有肿瘤疾病家族史：外祖母有输卵管癌疾病史，母亲有卵巢癌和乳腺癌病史，女方曾因“乳腺结节”行“右乳腺导管剥离+区段切除术”，术后诊断为“导管内乳头状瘤”。女方、外祖母和母亲均携带BRCA1基因c.5154G>A杂合突变。因夫妻双方有减少子代肿瘤尤其是乳腺癌患病风险的强烈意愿，经夫妻双方知情同意和浙江大学医学院附属妇产科医院生殖伦理委员会讨论通过后，决定采用PGT-M和PGT-P联合技术筛选乳腺癌低风险胚胎进行移植。 主要试剂和仪器 人绒毛膜促性腺激素2000 U（国药准字H20184171）为中国青岛冠龙生物制药有限公司产品；醋酸曲普瑞林注射液0.1 mg（国药准字H20223597）为中国重庆莱美药业股份有限公司产品；G1/G2培养基为瑞典Vitrolife公司产品；胚胎玻璃化冷冻为日本Kitazato公司产品；QIAamp DNA血液迷你试剂盒（51306）为德国Qiagen公司产品；MALBAC试剂盒（KT110700150）为中国上海亿康医学检验所有限公司产品。 构建乳腺癌多基因风险综合评估模型 基于UK Biobank（http：//www.ukbiobank.ac.uk/）中18 483例女性乳腺癌患者和246 222名对照者的遗传数据，参照文献［6，10］的方法，采用亚洲血统特异性SNP权重构建适用于亚洲人群的乳腺癌PRS313模型。考虑到乳腺癌发病的多因素特点，进一步基于同一数据集，参照文献［11］的建模方法，采用Cox比例风险回归法构建乳腺癌风险综合评估模型。该模型以生存函数为分析框架，将入组年龄、发病年龄和乳腺癌发生状态作为定义生存时间和结局的基础，纳入单基因致病变异携带状态、PRS313及乳腺癌一级亲属家族史作为协变量，评估不同协变量组合下的生存概率曲线及患病风险。基于上述模型，通过预测79岁前的生存概率估算各PRS百分位数对应的风险。考虑到各PRS百分位数内风险呈非正态分布，针对每0.01%的区间进行风险预测，并通过拟合指数曲线获得该百分位数内的风险变化速率，进而计算该百分位数的平均风险。 控制性卵巢刺激、胚胎培养和胚胎活检 夫妻双方知情同意后，患者予模拟黄体期方案促排卵，定期进行经阴道卵泡超声监测和血清内分泌水平检测，当一个优势卵泡直径发育到19~20 mm时予2000 IU人绒毛膜促性腺激素及0.1 mg醋酸曲普瑞林注射液扳机，36 h后行超声引导下经阴道穿刺取卵术。获取的卵子采用卵浆内单精子注射受精，在37 ng基因组DNA和胚胎活检标本使用MALBAC试剂盒进行全基因组扩增，随后按照制造商说明书对扩增产物进行文库构建。 PGT-A分析 将制备好的文库在Illumina HiSeq 2500平台上采用60碱基单端模式进行低深度全基因组测序（测序深度约0.1×，测序数据量约5 M读长），将高质量测序读段比对至人类基因组（hg19）。去除重复读段后，在整个基因组范围内以400 kb窗口进行读段计数。采用环形二元分割算法对读段计数进行鸟嘌呤（G）和胞嘧啶（C）含量标准化校正。将胚胎400 kb窗口的标准化读段数（R2）与参照文库对应窗口的标准化读段数（R1）进行比对（该参照文库基于100对男女样本的测序数据构建）。按下式计算胚胎各区域拷贝数：拷贝数=2×（R2÷R1）。拷贝数2.7及以上为重复，2.3~<2.7为嵌合重复，>1.7~<2.3为正常，1.7~>1.3为嵌合缺失，1.3及以下为缺失。通常报告大于4 Mb的重复/缺失区域，以及大于10 Mb的嵌合重复/缺失区域。 title: 537. Bridging the translational gap in psychiatry using a multimodal multi-omics collaboration: the consortium for preclinical psychiatric research
creator: S Sundram
description: BackgroundThere is a critical need to change the treatment paradigm for mental disorders by developing interventions that are able to target specific clinical components, alter the disease course and are not merely palliative in intent. A key strategy towards this goal is to focus research on causal pathways in mental disordersPMID:35026139.

title: Distinct immune cell dynamics associated with immune-related adverse events during combined chemoradiation and immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy
creator: Lei Zhang, Xiaokai Fan, Jun Ma, Jun Zhang, Ying Wei, Bin Hu, Di Zhou, Junjun Zhou, Yongrui Bai, Xiumei Ma, Jian Song, Jianming Tang, Haiyan Chen, Ying Jing
description: Combining chemoradiotherapy with immunotherapy increases the risk of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. To address this, we conducted a longitudinal single-cell multi-omics analysis of patients with locally advanced cervical cancer. Here we show that the proportions of CD4+ and CD8+ terminally differentiated effector memory or effector T cells are elevated in patients with irAEs.

title: In vitro exposure to non-antipseudomonal antibiotics (NAPA) induces Pseudomonas aeruginosa resistance to antipseudomonal antibiotics (APA)
creator: David Lasry, Luke B Harrison, Reggie Bamba, Rachel Corsini, Cedric P Yansouni, Matthew P Cheng, Todd C Lee, Alexander Lawandi
description: Background Pseudomonas aeruginosa readily evolves antimicrobial resistance through regulatory plasticity and stress-adaptive pathways. Clinically, antibiotics lacking intrinsic antipseudomonal activity are often favoured with the assumption that they avoid selective pressure on P. aeruginosa. Whether subinhibitory exposure to such ‘non-antipseudomonal antibiotics’ (NAPA) can nevertheless select for canonical resistance pathways remains incompletely defined.MethodsThree P.

title: 660. Irredeemably irremediable: consequences of colluding with hopelessness in non-terminal assisted dying provision
creator: K S Gaind
description: BackgroundPhysician Assisted Death (PAD) or Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD) has been legalized or decriminalized in over a dozen jurisdictions around the world. There is wide variation between policies, with most jurisdictions allowing for assisted dying only in terminal conditions, a minority allowing assisted dying outside end-of-life situations, and a smaller number allowing it for mental illness.

title: Biological and computer-aided evaluation of 3-methoxy-13α-estrone-16α-diphenylphosphine oxide as a new antiestrogenic agent
creator: Sándor Bartha, Péter Germán, Noémi Bózsity, László G Puskás, Rita Börzsei, Csaba Hetényi, István Zupkó, Erzsébet Mernyák, Renáta Minorics
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Breast cancer, a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, often depends on estrogen receptor alpha (ERα) signaling for progression. This study evaluates [(3-methoxy-17-oxo-13α-estra-1,3,5(10)-trien-16α-yl)methyl]diphenylphosphine oxide (EDPO), a recently published organophosphorus 13α-estrone derivative, as a potential antiestrogenic agent. In our previous study, EDPO showed substantial antiproliferative effect against T47D breast cancer cells and UPCI-SCC-131 oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma cells, with IC50 values of 7.2 µM and 5.3 µM, respectively.

title: Multicenter development and external validation of clinical–radiomics models to predict surgically confirmed upstaging in biopsy‐proven DCIS using DCE‐MRI
creator: Xi Hu, Lujie Qian, Jie He, Beili Shou, Ying Hu, Qingqing Chen, Enhui Xin, Fei Li, Zongyu Xie, Yue Qian, Feifei Lou, Nan Liu, Yu Kuang, Hongjie Hu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeDuctal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) diagnosed on core biopsy is frequently upgraded to invasive carcinoma at surgery, which may change indications for sentinel lymph node biopsy. Routine breast MRI has limited ability to detect occult invasion preoperatively. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an MRI‐based model combining clinical variables, conventional MRI findings, and dynamic contrast‐enhanced (DCE) MRI radiomics to predict invasive upgrade in biopsy‐proven DCIS.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study enrolled 478 patients from three hospitals (2014–2019).

title: 203. Sharpening focus: EEG evidence of attention network plasticity following adaptive working memory training in adult ADHD
creator: A Lintas, A Villa
description: BackgroundAdult Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is characterized by deficits in executive control and attention, accompanied by atypical electrophysiological activity within frontoparietal attention networks. These networks support alerting, orienting, and executive control functions and are commonly indexed by ERP components such as the N100 and P300.

title: Vaccinia virus mRNAs containing long 5′-poly(A)-leaders lack a canonical 5′-methylguanosine cap
creator: Václav Vopálenský, Michal Sýkora, Zora Mělková, Ivan Barvík, Kamila Horáčková, Tomáš Mašek, Martin Pospíšek
description: The vaccinia virus (VACV) is a prototypical poxvirus that was originally used to eradicate smallpox. Half a century ago, investigation into VACV mRNA substantially contributed to the fundamental discovery of the 5′ mRNA cap, a hallmark of all eukaryotic and many viral mRNAs. VACV research also facilitated the identification and understanding of the general mechanism of 5′ mRNA cap synthesis.

title: 569. Reviewing the evidence for sertraline in the treatment paradigm for premenstrual dysphoric disorder - an opportunity
creator: K Subramaniam, P Purushottamahanti, E F Chettiar
description: BackgroundSome women experience cognitive, affective and physical symptoms in the week before menses during the luteal cycle, that can range in severity [1]. Descriptions have evolved from “premenstrual tension” to “premenstrual syndrome” to a clearly defined “pre-menstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD)”, which is a severely disabling condition affecting 1.6% (31 million) females worldwide [2].

title: HighRes_Builder: improved access and modeling of noncanonical residues for protein structure prediction
creator: Yanchao Han, Jianfeng Mei, Gaoshuai Li, Enkang Dai, Hanlei Lu, Chengyun Zhang, Yanlu Zhang, Chenshui Lin, Chuanlong Zeng, Hongliang Duan, Xudong Wang
description: The growing support for noncanonical amino acids in structure prediction tools such as AlphaFold3 has been largely facilitated by the Chemical Component Dictionary (CCD). However, the limited coverage of modified residues in CCD continues to restrict the application of these models to many biologically and therapeutically relevant peptides.

title: The fru gene specifies male cooperative behaviors in honeybee colonies
creator: Sven Köhnen, Pia Ulbricht, Alina Sturm, Julie Carcaud, Jean-Christophe Sandoz, Thomas Eltz, Martin Beye
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Conspecific individuals can benefit from behavioral interactions, but whether cooperative behaviors require dedicated control in the nervous system is poorly understood. We examine the genetics underlying obligate cooperative male behaviors in honeybee colonies (Apis mellifera) that are deeply hardwired. We screened for transcription factor genes and found that only the fruitless (fru) BTB zinc-finger gene was restricted to expression in males and in the nervous system. Reporter coexpression revealed Fru-positive neuronal cell populations that are involved in processing and integrating sensory information.

title: 340. Synaptic density in psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders: a systematic review of in vivo SV2A PET studies
creator: G Mirfallah, C Schifani, D Shateri, R Sbrocca, G Bayraktar, A Mohiuddin, T Rodak, G Lo Buglio, B Jones, S Ameis, A Voineskos, M I Husain, G Foussias, M Solmi, M O Husain
description: BackgroundOver four decades of research have linked synaptic pathology to a broad range of brain disorders. Postmortem studies in conditions like psychosis spectrum disorders, Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) show changes in synaptic integrity but are confounded by factors such as illness duration or disease stage. Genetic research further suggests synaptic dysfunction via alterations in gene networks.

title: StackAge: an ensemble-based clock for precise quantification of biological age using multi-omics data
creator: Yingyi Jiang, Lei Jia, Yuan Fei, Xiaoguang Li, Xiaoqi Zheng, Yufang Qin
description: Accurate quantification of biological age is essential for early risk stratification and intervention of chronic diseases. Here, we present StackAge, an ensemble-based biological aging clock that integrates large-scale plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles from 30 376 participants in the UK Biobank. StackAge demonstrated high accuracy in age prediction (Pearson r ≈ 0.

title: FGF1-FGFR2 axis regulated by nuclear receptor RORγ represents an effective strategy in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
creator: Zhanfeng Gu, Xiaojuan Wang, Hong Wang, Junhua Wang, Zhaorong Huang, Dongyue Pan, Zhenhua Zhang, Yechun Zeng, Guodi Cai, Huizi Sun, Jun Zheng, Yichu Nie, Qingwen Zhang, Haolong Li, Franky Leung Chan, Junjian Wang, Jianwei Zheng, Yingfang Fan
description: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a highly aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Although targeted therapies like pemigatinib provide partial clinical benefits, acquired resistance remains a significant challenge. Through integrative bioinformatics analysis of public datasets and immunohistochemical validation, we identified the retinoid-related orphan receptor gamma (RORγ) as markedly upregulated in iCCA.

title: 419. A high-throughput screening platform for the discovery of selective M1/M4 muscarinic receptor agonists and positive allosteric modulators
creator: Z Yan, Y Zhang, H Tan, J Zhu, S Cui
description: BackgroundThe M1 and M4 subtypes of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (mAChRs) are compelling therapeutic targets for psychiatric disorders, as evidenced by the recent FDA approval of the M1/M4-preferring agonist xanomeline for schizophrenia. Achieving subtype selectivity is essential to obtain the procognitive and antipsychotic benefits of M1/M4 activation while minimize peripheral side effects mediated by M2/M3 receptors.

title: 824. Urticaria Associated with Polypharmacy Involving Quetiapine and Vortioxetine - A Case Report
creator: F Putri, K Runtuk
description: BackgroundAdvancing brain health together emphasises collaborative, patient-centred psychiatric care, particularly in the context of increasing psychotropic polypharmacy. Although combination therapy may enhance symptom control, it also increases the risk of adverse drug reactions. Cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions such as urticaria are uncommon but clinically significant and may compromise treatment adherence and patient safety.

title: QSyncFold: quantum neural network for multidimensional sync-discovery in protein folding
creator: Jinjing Shi, Peng Du, Wenwu Zeng, Wenxuan Wang, Shaoliang Peng, Xuelong Li
description: Quantum computing provides alternative encoding and sampling paradigms for protein structure prediction (PSP), but existing quantum-PSP methods are often limited by resource-scaling issues and by discrete or inefficient encodings for continuous coordinates. To address these limitations, we propose QSyncFold, a hybrid quantum–classical neural network framework that combines quantum superposition with differentiable learning.

title: TRIM24 promotes proliferation and metastasis of gastric cancer via mediating NRBP1 ubiquitination
creator: Chunyan Weng, Jingli Xu, Chenghai He, Rijuan Jin, Xiaoliang Jin, Shaopeng Sun, Siwei Pan, Meng Li, Yue Hu, Xi Wang, Yanqiang Zhang, Can Hu, Zhiyuan Xu, Bin Lv
description: The early detection and precise treatment of gastric cancer (GC) remain critical challenges worldwide. In this work, we screened and identified a subset of highly aggressive GC cell lines that exhibit elevated expression of TRIM24 using transwell assays and animal models. TRIM24 showed enhanced expression in GC cells and gastric carcinoma tissue samples in comparison with gastric noncancerous tissues.

title: The illusion of empowerment: commercializing women’s health in the digital age
creator: Brooke Nickel, Tessa Copp, Barbara Mintzes
description: l-Maharaj 2025), the knowledge gaps are well documented. However, alongside the advancement of the digital age, rapidly expanding commercial markets promise to close these gaps not through enhanced evidence and structural reform, but through products and services (McCarthy et al. 2023, Brassart Olsen 2024, Wood et al. 2025).

title: Age‐friendly environments and incident motoric cognitive risk syndrome in older adults: A prospective cohort study
creator: Hui Zhang, Zixin Hu, Chongyu Ding, Yaqian Xu, Shuai Jiang, Yi Li, Jiucun Wang, Xiaofeng Wang, Meng Hao, Xiangwei Li
description: INTRODUCTIONMotoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR) is a predementia condition that predicts multiple adverse health outcomes. Age‐friendly environments (AFE) represent a key strategy for promoting healthy aging and may reduce MCR risk. However, little is known about the association between AFE status and MCR risk.METHODSThis prospective cohort study used data from the National Health and Aging Trends Study.

title: Pan-cancer atlas analysis of FANCB and its potential mechanism in cholangiocarcinoma
creator: Youjie Fan, Jianhua Li, Haipeng Wang, Lei Yao, Xiaolei Wang
description: Cholangiocarcinoma (CHOL) is a tumor with high malignancy and poor prognosis, and its morbidity and mortality have increased significantly in China. The current therapeutic methods have limited efficacy and are easy to be resistant to drugs, and the targeted and immunotherapy still need precise strategy support.

title: 487. Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis reveals epigenetic signatures of early life stress in major depressive disorder patients
creator: Y Dwivedi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a pervasive condition, affecting over 20% of the global population. ELS, encompassing events like abuse and neglect, is a well-documented risk factor for the development of MDD in later life.

title: Does a Smarter ChatGPT Become More Utilitarian?
creator: Jürgen Pfeffer, Sebastian Krügel, Matthias Uhl
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hundreds of millions of users interact with large language models (LLMs) regularly to get advice on all aspects of life. The increase in LLMs’ logical capabilities might be accompanied by unintended side effects with ethical implications. Focusing on recent model developments of ChatGPT, we can show clear evidence for a systematic shift in ethical stances that accompanied a leap in the models’ logical capabilities.

title: Single-base resolution atlas reveals moderate conservation and regulatory diversity of m6A modifications across mammals
creator: Xiaoxiao Zhang, Zhan Zhang, Weiqiang Liu, Wenfu Liu, Meng Li, Weixiao Chen, Gaoming Liu, Yichen Dai, Zihao Li, Chunyan Hu, Qi Pan, Yang Yu, Xiangye Liu, Pingfen Zhu, Xuming Zhou
description: RNA methylation, notably m6A modification, is a predominant epitranscriptomic alteration in mRNA, yet its evolutionary properties and the selective constraints acting on it across mammals remain poorly understood. Here, we generated a single-base-resolution m6A modification atlas in liver, kidney, and brain tissues across 21 non-model mammals using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing. We found that 25.54–35.

title: 334. Restless legs syndrome induced by risperidone in adolescent: a case report
creator: K Saruhan
description: BackgroundRestless Leg Syndrome (RLS) is a neurological disorder that causes an urge to move the legs, accompanied by unpleasant sensations. Symptoms worsen during rest and improve with movement. It affects %5 of the population. The exact cause of primary RLS is unknown, but some theories suggest that it could be related to problems with iron metabolism or abnormal dopamine neurotransmission.

title: Correction to: Emergence and evolution of canonical microRNAs: A case study in Arabidopsis halleri and A. lyrata
creator: Unknown
description: t A. thaliana is the common ancestor of A. halleri and A. lyrata. Rather, A. lyrata and A. halleri are close living relatives of A. thaliana. A. lyrata and A. thaliana diverged from a common ancestor about 5 MYA, and A. halleri and A. lyrata diverged from each other about 1 MYA.

title: A cost- effectiveness and resource requirement comparison to optimize renal dialysis policies in Brunei Darussalam
creator: Aye Nandar Myint, Chiao Yuen Lim, Syukri Rahim, Lubna binti Haji Abdul Razak, Nor Islya Emma binti Othman, Siobhan Botwright, Waranya Rattanavipapong, Yot Teerawattananon
description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease is a growing global health concern, requiring kidney replacement therapy for survival. In Brunei, kidney failure incidence and prevalence are among the highest globally. Despite a peritoneal dialysis preference policy, uptake remains low, straining financial and human resources.

title: 854. The Future of Psychiatric Classification: Strategic Work On A New Diagnostic and Scientific Manual (DSM)
creator: J Alpert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) is widely used by healthcare providers. It is a common way for clinicians and researchers across disciplines to understand and codify mental and substance use disorders. In 2024, the American Psychiatric Association’s Board of Trustees approved the creation of a Future DSM Strategic Committee, tasked with monitoring scientific developments in the field that can impact the structure, definition, and criteria of disorders in the DSM.

title: 430. Investigating cellular phenotypes and genotypes of a preclinical model relevant to schizophrenia using single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: A Yonehara, A Coronado, A Gibbons, S Sundram, R Hill
description: BackgroundSchizophrenia is a highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by disruptions in cortical circuitry and excitatory-inhibitory balance. Converging genetic and post-mortem evidence implicates early dysfunction of GABAergic interneurons, and transcription factor ARX plays a critical role in interneuron differentiation and migration. Mutations in ARX are associated with a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders, including epilepsy, autism and schizophrenia.

title: Three-coordinated Ce(III) complexes with long wavelength d–f emissions
creator: Ziyu Liu, Yihu Yang, Wenliang Huang
description: Lanthanide luminescent materials have found a wide range of use in various fields. While most applications utilize intrashell f–f transitions, f–d transitions have recently emerged as a novel approach to develop molecular luminescent materials. Unlike Laporte-forbidden f–f transitions, f–d transitions are Laporte-allowed and thus not dependent on chromophoric ligands.

title: Associations of TyG-related indices with NAFLD-related outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Jinyang Li, Wantao Liu
description: Background:The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and related composite indices have been increasingly studied as accessible metabolic markers for fatty liver disease. However, evidence remains difficult to interpret because different TyG-related indices have been evaluated across heterogeneous populations and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD)-related outcomes.

title: 127. Lifestyle modification for panic disorder treatment: a three-year cohort study through wearable monitoring, AI, and case management system
creator: C Tsai
description: BackgroundPanic disorder (PD) is a recurrent and often debilitating anxiety condition characterized by sudden episodes of intense fear and physiological arousal. Despite the availability of pharmacological and psychotherapeutic treatments, many individuals continue to experience persistent symptoms, low treatment adherence, and high relapse rates after initial improvement.

title: Phenology modulates the top-down control of ants on bird ectoparasites: from mutualism to antagonism
creator: Jesús M Avilés, Ángela Salido, Joaquín L Reyes-López, Deseada Parejo
description: Bird–ant interactions are diverse but rarely tested experimentally, limiting their integration into ecological theory. One hypothesized but unverified benefit is ant-mediated parasite control in bird nests. Here, we present the first experimental evidence supporting this hypothesis in a wild system involving house sparrows (Passer domesticus), arboreal ants (Crematogaster scutellaris), and blood-feeding mites (Pellonyssus reedi).

title: 818. Exercise-Induced Modulation of Glymphatic Function Assessed by Diffusion Tensor Imaging–ALPS in Healthy Adults
creator: M Abdullah, S-H Lin, L-C Huang, Y K Yang
description: BackgroundPhysical exercise exerts robust neuroprotective and neuromodulatory effects in both healthy and clinical populations.
